value-in-db: capex 1744 CAD/t-yr; cost-levelized 1627 CAD/t; SEC 20.3 GJ/t; emissions-total 1.28 t/t
issue: Most of the pooled examples are explicitly per tonne of ethylene, not per tonne of high-value chemicals, and no conversion is applied. Layritz 2021 capex (3031) and levelized cost (1325) are per t ethylene capacity, every van-geene_2024 (MIDDEN) cracker row is derived from MEUR per kt ethylene/yr (TC0263, TC0265, TC0431, TC0433), Boulamanti 2017 SEC, emissions and capex rows say per t ethylene, Mynko 2023 divides by ethylene tonnes, and Saygin 2011 uses its Ethylene row. Boulamanti's own per-t-HVC twins sit unused in _other-values.
benchmark: HVC per tonne of ethylene is about 1.6-1.8 for a naphtha cracker and about 1.2 for an ethane cracker, so the per-t-HVC values should be roughly 1.3-1.8x lower: capex about 1000-1300 CAD/t-yr, SEC about 13-17 GJ/t HVC, direct CO2 about 0.7-1.0 t/t HVC.
recommendation: Convert every per-t-ethylene example to the HVC basis with a feed-specific yield, or switch to the per-t-HVC rows the same sources print (Boulamanti _other-values, IEA 2018). Ask Brad to set one yield per feedstock.

issue: Saygin 2011 Table 1 prints its Steam column as a net steam export (negative), and the loader keeps the sign as a steam consumption. The cracker takes -1.4 (saygin_2011_001, Ethylene row) and the ammonia efficiency-strong archetype -3.9 (same table, Ammonia from natural gas row). The ccs-diffuse variant then adds the capture reboiler duty of 0.2084 GJ/t to -1.4 and lands at -1.19, so a cracker that is running an amine plant still reports a net steam export.
benchmark: A steam carrier should be a demand. A cracker with flue-gas capture needs roughly +1 to +2 GJ/t of reboiler steam; the export credit of 1.4-3.9 GJ/t belongs in a separate by-product or steam-export flow.
recommendation: Move the negative Saygin values to an export flow (or exclude them) so the steam carrier stays non-negative, and let the ccs-energy rule add the capture duty to a zero or positive base.

issue: The heat carrier (rehfeldt_2024_001 p.49, n=1) is 1.8x the untagged total of 20.3 GJ/t and 1.8x the fuel carrier of 20.0 GJ/t, so the carrier set cannot be summed. The source states it is process heat per t ethylene. The previous pass recorded this as R472 and the build still shows it.
benchmark: Cracker process heat is about 13-20 GJ/t HVC, which is already in the fuel and process-off-gas carriers; a separate heat row on top double counts.
recommendation: Drop the Rehfeldt row from the heat carrier, or convert it to the HVC basis and record it as the fuel-equivalent instead of a second carrier. See R472 in docs/sanity-checks/2026-10-04/review.csv.

issue: The ccs-host-plus-addon-energy rule spreads the 1.465 GJ/t capture add-on across the carrier mix of the capture node pool, which gives a naphtha steam cracker a coal demand of 0.214 GJ/t and an unnamed not-stated demand of 0.239 GJ/t. Only 0.208 of the 1.465 GJ/t reaches the steam carrier, where an amine reboiler duty belongs.
benchmark: A post-combustion amine unit on a cracker uses about 2.3 GJ of low-pressure steam and 0.1-0.15 GJ of electricity per t CO2 captured; none of it is coal.
recommendation: Fix the rule so the add-on is split over the host's own carriers (steam and electricity), not the capture node's, and suppress carriers the host does not list.

issue: The untagged total comes from one example, doe_2015_004 Table A1a state-of-the-art 3138 Btu/lb, which is onsite energy excluding the natural-gas feedstock. The same archetype's natural-gas carrier is 29.96 GJ/t and its base archetype steam-reformer_ammonia is 31.07 GJ/t, so the model reads a 76% energy saving from an efficiency variant. The IEA 2013 rows on this archetype show the two bases side by side (28-33 GJ/t with feedstock, 7.5-12 without). Recorded as R485 in the previous pass and still present.
benchmark: Best-practice ammonia from natural gas is 28-32 GJ/t NH3 HHV including feedstock; the thermodynamic minimum is about 20 GJ/t. A plant total below 10 GJ/t is impossible.
recommendation: Exclude the feedstock-free DOE and IEA totals from the untagged total, or tag them with a feedstock-excluded flag so they pool separately. See R485.

issue: The only example (jrc_2007_002 p.65) is 31.1 GJ/t fuel plus feed after revamping a plant commissioned in 1971, which the build converts LHV to HHV to 34.51. That is above the base archetype steam-reformer_ammonia at 31.07 GJ/t, so the moderate efficiency variant uses more energy than the plant it improves (screen-variant flags it).
benchmark: The same JRC page gives the pre-revamp value of 36.0 GJ/t and a net 30.6 GJ/t after revamp; a moderate variant should sit a few per cent below the base, so about 28-30 GJ/t HHV.
recommendation: Record the JRC pair as an increment (36.0 before, 31.1 after) rather than as the variant's level, or use the net 30.6 GJ/t. Ask Brad which the model needs.

issue: The archetype is defined as capture on the process CO2, which the host records as 1.25 t/t of a 1.93 t/t total. The captured value of 1.5 t/t (gielen_1997_001 p.13, Table 2.1.5, a 1997 MARKAL input whose design also strips flue gas) is larger than the stream the archetype captures, and the derived share-to-capture of 86.36% follows from it (1.5 / (0.9 x 1.93)). This is the open item from the brief, now 86% rather than 99%.
benchmark: Process-CO2-only capture on an SMR ammonia plant is 55-65% of plant CO2 (material-economics_2019_001 p.148: 55% process, about 64% with hydrogen-rich burner fuel; collodi_2010_001: 60%), so captured should be about 1.1-1.25 t/t and the share about 60%.
recommendation: Set emissions-captured to the host's process CO2 (about 1.25 t/t) or exclude the Gielen row, and let share-to-capture follow; keep the 81-90% figures for a whole-plant capture variant.

issue: The single example is martin_2000_001 p.81 (Chemicals-7), 55 USD2000 per short ton of annual capacity, and its own note records the source cost type as Retrofit. An incremental retrofit figure is being used as the whole-plant capex, and it then seeds the CCS variant (562 CAD/t-yr), the levelized costs and the family capex median. The previous pass recorded this as R492 for the predecessor archetype and the build still shows it.
benchmark: A greenfield ATR-based ammonia plant is about 1500-2500 CAD per t NH3 per year; the sibling steam-reformer_ammonia carries 832 and gasifier_coal-ammonia 1900.
recommendation: Set the Martin row aside as incremental and name a host, or replace it with a greenfield ATR ammonia capex. See R492.

value-in-db: total 0.311 t/t; process 0.54 t/t; captured 0.140 t/t
issue: The host's total direct CO2 (0.311 t/t, van-geene_2024_001 TC0267) is below its own process CO2e of 0.54 t/t (boulamanti_2017_001 Table 75), which cannot hold on one basis: MIDDEN's figure is for its Dutch reference plant at 89% conversion while Boulamanti's is per t EO at 80% selectivity. The capture variant inherits the small total, and with Boulamanti's 50% share (his own stated assumption for lack of data) captures only 0.140 t/t of a 0.5 t/t concentrated scrubber stream.
benchmark: EO process CO2 is 0.22-0.86 t/t EO depending on selectivity (falcke_2017_001), and a concentrated capture on the CO2 scrubber vent should take 80-90% of it, so about 0.4-0.5 t/t.
recommendation: Put the MIDDEN and Boulamanti rows on one product basis (t EO) before pooling, then raise the capture share from Boulamanti's placeholder 50%.

issue: The single example is ren_2009_001 p.63 Table 3-6 at 0.042 t CO2/GJ, converted with a 22.7 GJ/t energy figure (the thesis's primary-energy intensity) rather than this archetype's 11.4 GJ/t. The result, 0.952 t/t, is 1.7x the archetype's own total direct CO2 of 0.57 t/t (van-geene_2024_001 TC0174), so combustion exceeds the total.
benchmark: A natural-gas methanol plant emits about 0.5-0.7 t CO2/t methanol in total, of which roughly 0.2-0.3 t/t is reformer and utility combustion.
recommendation: Re-derive the Ren factor against this archetype's SEC on a final-energy basis, or exclude the row and let the total carry the emissions.

issue: The untagged total is Negri 2021's 8 MJ/kg of light olefins, which is gasification process energy only, while the biomass carrier is joosten_1998_001 Table 21 (52.5 GJ/t) and material-economics_2019_001 Exhibit 3.12 (66 GJ/t), both of which are the biomass feedstock. The total is 6.6x below its own carrier sum. The previous pass recorded this as R420 and the build still shows it.
benchmark: Biomass to olefins needs about 50-70 GJ/t HVC of biomass including feedstock, or about 8-12 GJ/t of process energy excluding it. The two cannot share one parameter.
recommendation: Separate feedstock from process energy (a feedstock flag or a feedstock flow), and note that Joosten is per t ethylene, not per t HVC. See R420.

value-in-db: total 0.498 GJ/t; electricity 0.504 GJ/t; heat 2.88 GJ/t
issue: The untagged total is one MIDDEN card (van-geene_2024_001 TC0177) while the carriers come from kiss_2017_001 Table 10.1 for a vapour-recompressed dividing-wall ethanol column. The total is below its own electricity carrier and 6.8x below the carrier sum, and the 2.88 GJ/t heat row is the reboiler duty of the baseline column, which a heat-pumped column should largely not need. R406 and R408 in the previous pass; still present.
benchmark: A heat-pumped or MVR column uses about 0.4-0.7 GJ/t of electricity and little or no reboiler steam; total energy about 0.5-1.0 GJ/t.
recommendation: Put the total and the carriers on one example set (the Kiss VRC case), and drop or re-label the 2.88 GJ/t baseline reboiler duty. See R406 and R408.

issue: The heat-pumped column carries a unit-level capex of 86.6 CAD/t-yr while its conventional sibling distillation-column carries a whole-plant 1060 CAD/t-yr, so the model sees the heat-pumped option as twelve times cheaper than the column it replaces. The previous pass recorded the unit-versus-plant mix as R401 for distillation-column_fired-heater and the same mismatch now sits across these two archetypes.
benchmark: Vapour-recompression retrofits on a distillation train cost roughly 100-400 CAD per t-yr as an increment; a whole distillation train is roughly 500-1100 CAD per t-yr. The two archetypes must share a scope.
recommendation: Decide one scope for the distillation family (whole train or column unit) and re-scope the examples, or name a host plant so the increment can be added to it. Ask Brad. See R401 and open item S27.

issue: Two rows from the same source and pass (boulamanti_2017_001) contradict each other: emissions-process n2o is 0.3 t/t, which is 79-89 t CO2e/t at GWP 265-298, while emissions-process co2e is 32 t/t. The 32 t/t then propagates into emissions-total through the sum identity. R427 in the previous pass; still present.
benchmark: Unabated adipic acid is about 0.3 t N2O/t, that is 80-90 t CO2e/t; an abated European plant is about 2-10 t CO2e/t. 32 t/t matches neither and looks like a partly-abated average.
recommendation: Derive emissions-process co2e from the n2o row and the chosen GWP rather than pooling the source's own co2e, and decide whether the archetype is abated or unabated. Ask Brad. See R427.

issue: The identity adds the coal SEC (5.82277 GJ/t, ieaghg_2008_001, tp-ieaghg_2008_001-0024) and the natural-gas SEC (4.38925 GJ/t, hughes_2023_001 and voldsund_2019_001) as if the unit burned both. 5.82277 x 0.0889 + 4.38925 x 0.05064 = 0.740 reproduces the value exactly. Coal and gas are alternative ways of raising the same reboiler steam, so only one belongs in the sum. The result also contradicts emissions-total -0.9 t/t on the same archetype.
benchmark: Gas-fired reboiler steam at 4.39 GJ/t x 0.0506 = 0.22 t CO2/t captured; coal-fired 5.82 x 0.0889 = 0.52 t/t. Either, not both.
recommendation: Fix the fuel-emission-factor rule so it picks one fossil carrier (the highest-ranked, or the archetype's named carrier) rather than summing every fossil carrier present; then re-derive emissions-total so the two rows close.

issue: The inverse identity reads the total SEC, 0.269892 GJ/GJ, as a conversion input. That SEC is the liquefier's parasitic electricity (10.63 kWh/kg from ANL HDSAM, record tp-anl_2025_001-0010), not hydrogen converted into hydrogen. The archetype's own description says liquefaction takes about a third of the hydrogen's energy, so 1/0.27 is meaningless.
benchmark: About 79 % on an energy-in over energy-out basis (1/(1+0.27)); better still, no efficiency at all for a conditioning step.
recommendation: Add a condition to id-efficiency-from-sec: do not fire where the SEC carrier set excludes the product carrier, that is on conditioning, transport, and storage archetypes (liquefaction-train, pipeline, storage-cavern, compressor). Leave efficiency unfilled here.

issue: Two Neuwahl 2019 rows (tp-neuwahl_2019_001-0032 electricity 0.107 MWh/t MSW and -0033 heat 0.505 MWh/t MSW) are the incineration plant's own auxiliary demands per tonne of waste. They were normalised by an MSW energy content of about 7.1 GJ/t, so they sit per GJ of waste in, while the archetype is per GJ of heat out. The inverse identity then returns 1/0.31031 = 322 %. The archetype description also says per t of waste while product-unit is GJ of heat.
benchmark: WtE net electrical efficiency 18-28 % and total CHP efficiency 60-85 % (WI BREF 2019); the sibling efficiency [electricity] already reads 30.9 %.
recommendation: Re-scope the two Neuwahl rows onto a per-GJ-heat-out basis or set them aside; block the inverse identity here; reconcile the description with product-unit GJ heat. Extends R073 of the 2026-10-04 pass, which flagged the heat row as likely an output.

value-in-db: no row; total 1.65356 GJ/GJ, carriers only heat 0.141054 and electricity 0.00874533
issue: The only all-carrier example (tp-van-geene_2024_001-0869, 211.3 GJ/t H2) includes the natural-gas feedstock, but no natural-gas carrier row exists, so the carrier split sums to 0.150 against a total of 1.654 (screen-carriers ratio 0.091). A model reading the carriers sees an ATR running on 0.15 GJ of input per GJ of hydrogen. The _ccs-concentrated sibling does carry fuel 1.29987, so the unabated base looks better than the capture case.
benchmark: ATR hydrogen: 1.3-1.6 GJ natural gas (feedstock plus fuel) per GJ of H2 HHV; the archetype's own efficiency of 72 % implies 1.39 GJ/GJ.
recommendation: Add a natural-gas carrier row derived from the total less the named carriers, or carry the sibling's 1.30 GJ/GJ across. Same class as open item S98.

issue: The biomass feedstock row is far short of a gasification feed. The NREL H2A rows behind it (nrel_2009_001, nrel_2018_003) are auxiliary energy, not the feed, and the untagged total repeats the same magnitude, so nothing carries the biomass. The archetype's own efficiency, 43.8 %, implies 2.28 GJ of biomass per GJ of H2.
benchmark: Biomass-to-hydrogen gasification: 1.5-2.5 GJ biomass per GJ H2 HHV.
recommendation: Re-extract the H2A feedstock line for both NREL cases and set the biomass carrier from it, or derive the biomass SEC from the sourced efficiency. Still present from R164 of the 2026-10-04 pass (then 0.079 GJ/GJ at 64.8 % efficiency).

issue: The archetype's carriers list names electricity, which is its product, not its input. The split therefore copied the preheat-fuel figure (1.17228 GJ/GJ, hedman_2008_001 range midpoint) onto electricity, so the device consumes 1.17 GJ of electricity per GJ of electricity it makes. screen-carriers flags the sum at 2.25x the total. It also inflates cost-levelized [calculated-incl-energy] to 85 CAD/GJ.
benchmark: The input carrier is natural gas for line heating at 1-2 GJ/GJ (settled in R563); an electricity SEC should be absent or a few per cent for auxiliaries.
recommendation: Change the carriers list to natural-gas (line heating) so single-carrier-split lands on the right carrier, and drop the electricity row. Same class as open item S94 on wrong carriers lists.

value-in-db: 9.13242 years (80,000 h), low 1.14155 (10,000 h), high 9.13242, n=4, central-from top-ranked: IRENA 2020
issue: IRENA 2020 prints two SOEC stack lives and the ranker took the 2050 target (tp-irena_2020_001-0052, 80,000 h) over the 2020 state of the art in the same table (tp-irena_2020_001-0045, 20,000 h). The species also mixes bases: the IRENA and IEA rows are operating hours divided by 8760, while nrel_2026_001 row -0082 is a 4-year calendar replacement interval.
benchmark: SOEC stack life today 10,000-30,000 h (IRENA 2020 Table 6, IEA 2019 Table 3); 80,000 h is a 2050 target.
recommendation: Prefer the state-of-the-art row over the target row when a source prints both, and keep hours-based and calendar-year lifetimes in separate species. Follows the fix recorded against S74 and R004.

issue: The central is the only point value among the untagged examples: tp-doe_2024_002-0018, 1,106 USD/t, a levelized cost of avoided CO2 against a 70 %-efficient gas boiler on a declining grid-intensity path. The three other untagged examples (agora_2021_001 -54 to +131 EUR/t, doe_2023_001 -6 to +14 USD/t, zuberi_2022_002 67-185 USD/t) are range-only, so they never reach the central.
benchmark: Electric-boiler abatement cost 0-250 CAD/t on Canadian power-to-gas price spreads; Agora and DOE 2023 both straddle zero.
recommendation: Take the midpoints of the three range-only examples into the pool so the median is not a single corner case, and flag the DOE 2024 scenario value. The separate [co2] target carries 16-543 CAD/t; merge the two targets. R028 of 2026-10-04 raised the same problem on the [co2] target and it is still open.

issue: Negative energy consumption. The pool holds four values on two different bases: doe_2015_001 -0.35 (tp-doe_2015_001-0014, state-of-the-art net intensity), worrell_2010_001 -0.30 (tp-worrell_2010_001-0017, overall energy surplus taking recovered energy into account), pardo_2013_001 -1.761 (tp-pardo_2013_001-0055, Table 1 current process -0.853 plus the Table 2 BAT change -0.908), and the UKERC saving on the base archetype 0.225 (tp-epa_2012_001-s005). The median of the four is -0.325. Three of the four are net of BOF gas and sensible heat recovery; the fourth is a gross input.
benchmark: Gross energy input to a BOF with gas recovery is 0.2 to 0.5 GJ/t liquid steel; the recovery credit (BOF gas 70-100 Nm3/t at 7-8 MJ/Nm3 plus steam) is at most about -1.0 GJ/t and belongs on an export flow, not in SEC
recommendation: Split the basis: keep SEC as gross input on both the base and the variant, and record BOF gas and steam recovery as a by-product flow. If the net convention is kept deliberately, say so in docs/design.md and stop the levelized-cost and CO2 identity rules from reading a negative SEC. Still present from R218 and R219 of the 2026-10-04 pass.

issue: The MIDDEN coke-plant card is in the database twice and only one copy was excluded. tp-van-geene_2024_001-0099 (TC0022) carries the ruling that the derived 40.8 GJ/t counts the coking coal fed, so it is feedstock plus process energy (sanity-check R246, modeller 2026-10-05). Its twin tp-van-geene_2024_001-0131 (TC0031, coke plant for TGR-CCS) has the identical value, formula, and locator sheet but no exclusion, so it still pools. It sets the high to 42.9 and lifts the central off the documented 6.70.
benchmark: Process energy for a by-product coke oven is 4 to 7 GJ/t coke; the documented central for this build is 6.70 (median of DOE 2015, Golder, Hasanbeigi, and Pardo)
recommendation: Exclude tp-van-geene_2024_001-0131 on the same ruling as -0099, and make the exclusion rule match on the source and the derivation rather than on the single record id. This also drags the carrier bands: because the carriers are a share of the total, the bad high propagates to fuel 41.78, coke-oven-gas 25.01, and blast-furnace-gas 16.78 GJ/t. Sanity-check item S12 covers the central but recorded the exclusion as done.

value-in-db: 1.29685 GJ/t (n=1) in wide-archetype.csv; a second row holds 13.6838-14.7364 with no central
issue: Two rows share the key archetype plus parameter plus empty target. One is graded range only (hasanbeigi_2013_001 and hasanbeigi_2014_001, 13-14 GJ/t hot metal) with no central; the other is the sum of the carriers of de Beer et al. 1998 (1.29685) with no band. wide-archetype.csv takes the second and drops the range, so the modeller view says a smelting-reduction vessel uses 1.3 GJ/t hot metal.
benchmark: COREX, HIsarna, and similar smelting reduction use 13 to 20 GJ/t hot metal before any export-gas credit (Hasanbeigi 13-14; Remus 17; Gielen 20-29 coal)
recommendation: Fix the duplicate key in the pooling stage: one row per archetype, parameter, and target, with the range-only row supplying the band when the carrier sum supplies the central. Here the carrier sum must not stand as the total at all (see IS005). The CCS child smelting-vessel_smelting-reduction_ccs-concentrated inherits the error at 3.14485 GJ/t.

issue: The central is 15 to 30 times below every one of the 11 coal examples behind it. central-from reads share 96.3% of fuel, split from de Beer et al. 1998 (tp-de-beer_1998_001-0019). That de Beer row is Other fuel 1.02 GJ/thm from Table 8, which sits beside the coal input rows in the same table (tp-de-beer_1998_001-0001, -0010, -0014, -0018, -0024: 18.6 to 43.2 GJ/t). The split rule took the one fuel row that excludes coal as the whole fuel total, so coal ends up at 4% of a value that was never the fuel total.
benchmark: Coal to a smelting-reduction vessel is 15 to 30 GJ/t hot metal (de Beer 18.6-43.2, Gielen 21-30, Remus 17.9, Worrell net 15-17)
recommendation: Make the carrier-split reference example one whose carrier rows add up to its own total, or fall back to the carrier medians when they do not. Here the de Beer Other fuel row should not be read as the fuel total.

issue: The class-median fill writes the low band as a fraction while the central is a percentage, so the low is 100 times too small (0.972603 reads as 355/365). It then propagates: annual-output low becomes capacity times 0.0097 (annealing-furnace_batch-bell 42.6 t/yr against a central of 3,942; basic-oxygen-furnace_efficiency-strong 42,308 t/yr against 3.9 Mt), and cost-levelized high divides by it, giving basic-oxygen-furnace_efficiency-strong 4.56e8 2025_CAD/t and ten more archetypes in this family at 12,000 to 69,000 CAD/t.
benchmark: A capacity-factor band on an industrial furnace is roughly 60 to 100 %; the levelized-cost high should stay within a few times the central
recommendation: Fix the unit in the class-median capacity-factor fill (multiply the low by 100, or store capacity factor as a fraction everywhere), then rebuild annual-output and cost-levelized. Affects every family, not just this one.

issue: The central is the single lowest example, picked by source rank rather than by median: central-from reads top-ranked: Van Geene et al. 2024 (MIDDEN), tp-van-geene_2024_001-0108. It is 30 times below the archetypes own emissions-combustion (0.2466) and process (0.11) rows, so the total is far below each of its parts. Pardo 0.181 is in the pool; Moya was set aside as the duplicate JRC paper, which left MIDDEN top-ranked.
benchmark: BOF direct CO2 is 0.15 to 0.25 t/t liquid steel (Pardo 0.181; IS BREF 0.1-0.2). MIDDEN 0.008 excludes the decarburisation CO2 that leaves in the BOF gas.
recommendation: Exclude or re-scope tp-van-geene_2024_001-0108, or require emissions-total to be at least the sum of its sourced parts. The 2026-10-04 pass recorded this as R217 with central 0.181; the central has since moved down to 0.008, so the build got worse.

issue: The untagged total comes from one example about a different product: worrell_2000_001:air-separation-unit_nitrogen, a preliminary SEC including feedstock from a key-chemicals table, on an archetype whose product is a tonne of oxygen. The electricity carrier is then derived as share 92.2% of that total, so 1.66 GJ/t overrides the seven direct oxygen measurements behind it (ieaghg_2013_003 1.386 and 1.184, smith_2001_001 1.338, daniels_2002_001 1.7 and 1.1, ieaghg_2008_001 0.874 and 0.72-0.864), whose median is about 1.13.
benchmark: Cryogenic ASU 160 to 320 kWh/t O2, that is 0.58 to 1.15 GJ/t of gaseous oxygen
recommendation: Drop or re-scope the nitrogen example as the oxygen total, and let the electricity carrier pool its own seven examples. The 2026-10-04 pass raised the same total as R210 and the carrier as R209 at 1.26 GJ/t; the carrier-split change of 2026-10-05 (S82) has since pushed it up to 1.66, so the fix for S82 made this one worse.

issue: An efficient variant that emits 64% more than its host. The carrier split is a judgement that rewrites the fuel mix rather than taking a saving on the hosts mix: coke 8.91, coal 2.88, natural gas 1.31, with the rationale split 68/22/10 as a typical Canadian furnace with gas injection. The host blast-furnace is coke 11.98, coal 1.57, natural gas 0.236. id-combustion-co2-from-fuel then reads the richer coal and gas shares and returns 1.304 against the hosts 0.7934.
benchmark: A moderate-efficiency blast furnace should emit at or below the host, about 0.7 to 1.1 t CO2/t iron from combustion
recommendation: Derive a variants carrier split from its hosts split scaled to the variants total, and keep the judgement split only where the host has none. Then re-run the CO2 identity.

issue: The band mixes with-capture and without-capture configurations. tp-van-geene_2024_001-0128 gives 0.0489 t/t, the residual of a MIDDEN TGR plant with CCS (its SEC twin tp-van-geene_2024_001-0127 was excluded), while otto_2017_001 gives 0.392 and 1.065 for two TGR cases. This archetype is TGR without capture, so the 0.049 end does not belong in it.
benchmark: TGR-BF without capture about 1.0 to 1.2 t CO2/t hot metal; with capture about 0.4 to 0.6 residual
recommendation: Exclude the MIDDEN with-capture residual from this archetype, or create the TGR-with-capture variant it belongs to. Raised as R232 on 2026-10-04 and still present, though the central has moved off 0.0489.

issue: A per-tonne-of-crude-steel value on an archetype whose product unit is a tonne of CO2. tp-draxler_2021_001-0019 is 3.6 MWh/t crude steel at full maturity; the identical 3.6 MWh/t from tp-agora_2021_001-0033 was excluded under S80 as a whole-route per-t-crude-steel value, but the Draxler copy was not. The total then equals the electricity row alone, with no fuel, and capex 4,458 CAD/t-per-yr from almeida-benalcazar_2022_001 looks to be per tonne of the chemical product rather than per tonne of CO2.
benchmark: Steel off-gas to chemicals needs roughly 1.5 to 3 GJ of electricity plus 2 to 6 GJ of steam per t CO2 converted; a value per t crude steel is about 2 t CO2 larger per unit
recommendation: Apply the S80 set-aside to tp-draxler_2021_001-0019 as well, and re-base the Almeida-Benalcazar cost rows to the declared product unit. Related to open item S98.

issue: Both carry Gielen 1997 Table 2.7.4/2.7.5 variable O&M of 250 ECU/t, which includes labour and is a whole-product cost. The 2026-10-04 pass ruled this out (R351, R366) but the exclusion landed only on the year-2000 records; the identical year-2050 records (tp-gielen_1997_001-0288 and -0306) are still live and set the pooled central.
benchmark: Furnace-level non-energy variable opex 10-30 CAD/t; full container-glass production cost 250-450 CAD/t
recommendation: Exclude tp-gielen_1997_001-0288 and -0306 as well, or rule out the whole Gielen variable-O&M column; then re-derive furnace_regenerative_ccs-diffuse, which inherits it through the ccs-cost rule. R351 and R366 are not fixed in this build.

issue: Same Gielen 1997 variable-O&M column. The high comes from tp-gielen_1997_001-0208, ceramic tiles at 600 ECU/t (1678.73 CAD/t), which is a whole-product cost many times a tile's value; the central comes from the bricks row at 15 ECU/t.
benchmark: Kiln-level non-energy variable opex for structural ceramics 5-20 CAD/t
recommendation: Exclude tp-gielen_1997_001-0208 with the other Gielen whole-product O&M rows, and re-check the central against a non-Gielen source.

value-in-db: kiln emissions-total 0.82 t/t clinker; opex-fixed and levelized cost per t
issue: Many examples state their figure per tonne of CEMENT but are pooled into kiln archetypes whose product is clinker, with no rebase correction. Clear cases: agora_2021_001 (combustion 0.21 t/t, oxy-fuel total 0.06 t/t, oxy-fuel electricity 0.25 MWh/t), emanuelsson_2022_001 (0.7 and 0.07 t/t, opex 17 and 19 EUR/t), doe_2023_002 (0.7751 emitted and 0.7363 captured, note says per t cement), ieaghg_2008_001 and material-economics_2019_001 levelized costs, rootzen_2017_001 and vattenfall_2018_001 fixed opex, worrell_2022_001 62 kWh/t. Only five ETSAP I03 rows carry the rebase (sc-038 to sc-042). The reverse case also occurs: nedo_2008_001 and martin_1999_001 give finish-mill power per t clinker or per t meal, pooled into mills whose product is cement.
benchmark: A dry precalciner kiln emits 0.84-0.88 t CO2 per t clinker (0.52-0.53 process plus 0.31-0.35 fuel); per t cement the same plant is about 10% lower at a 0.91 clinker factor. The pooled 0.82 sits below the clinker-basis range.
recommendation: Extend the rebase correction (factor cf-clinker-per-cement-etsap-i03 or each source's own clinker factor) to these rows, and apply it the other way for the mill rows stated per t clinker or per t raw meal. Ask Brad whether a product-basis field on the example row would be cheaper than one correction per row.

issue: The high comes from tp-etsap_2010_003-0035, a high-pressure roll mill printed as 445 kWh/t of cement in ETSAP I03 p.5. Every other source in the pool gives 14-50 kWh/t. This looks like the same kind of decimal or row slip already corrected in ETSAP I03 under sc-007 and sc-008.
benchmark: Finish grinding 20-50 kWh/t cement (0.07-0.18 GJ/t); HPGR and roller presses at the low end
recommendation: Read 445 as 44.5 kWh/t under a new source correction, or exclude the record; either way the high falls to about 0.2 GJ/t. Also sanity-check the 50.5 kWh/t ETSAP row that sets the central, since a vertical roller mill should sit below the ball mill at 0.229 GJ/t, not alongside it.

value-in-db: 4.08 GJ/t against a total of 0.221 GJ/t
issue: The total pools three van-geene_2024_001 asphalt cards (electric rotary drum, 0.203-0.257 GJ per t of aggregate) while the only carrier row, tp-martin_2000_002-0087, is an infrared dryer at 4.08 GJ per t of PAPER. Two different products in one archetype; central-from records the disagreement rather than resolving it.
benchmark: An electric dryer's electricity use equals its total, so the two rows should agree. Paper drying at 4 GJ/t belongs with the pulp-and-paper dryers.
recommendation: Move the martin_2000_002 infrared row to the pulp-and-paper paper dryer, or exclude it here; the carrier row then follows the total.

issue: Both highs come from one van-geene_2024_001 card, TC0070 glass-wool production with an electric furnace (tp-van-geene_2024_001-0244 and -0245). That card is a whole glass-wool plant per t of product, including fiberising and curing, not melting per t of melt. An all-electric furnace also cannot emit 0.477 t CO2 per t of melt.
benchmark: All-electric melting 2.9-4.5 GJ/t melt for container and flat glass; process CO2 from carbonates 0.03-0.2 t/t
recommendation: Set aside TC0070 for this archetype, or give glass-wool production its own archetype. The 6.5-16.5 GJ/t high-temperature insulation wool rows in scalet_2013_001 deserve the same treatment.

issue: The high is tp-doe_2017_003-0187, edible rendering of lard and tallow at 4,573 Btu per lb of rendered fat. That is a whole-process intensity on a different product, 32 times the central, and it sets the band for the whole archetype and for its efficiency-strong variant.
benchmark: Steam-heated thermal processing in food and drink 0.1-1.0 GJ per t of product
recommendation: Exclude or set aside the rendering row; the band then closes to about 0.03-0.8 GJ/t.

value-in-db: 0.1188 GJ/t, all electricity; combustion CO2 0; abatement cost -95.7 CAD/t
issue: The only energy example (sanchez-berriel_2016_001) gives grinding electricity, so the archetype lists no fuel carrier, and the zero-if-no-fossil identity then sets combustion CO2 to zero. Calcining the clay at 700-850 degC is the whole point of LC3 and is missing, which is also why the abatement cost comes out strongly negative.
benchmark: LC3 or calcined-clay cement needs about 2.0-2.5 GJ/t cement of thermal energy, of which 0.5-0.9 GJ/t is clay calcination, plus 0.1-0.15 GJ/t of grinding electricity
recommendation: Re-extract the calcination fuel from Sanchez Berriel 2016 or add a clay-calcination example, then re-run the combustion identity and the abatement cost. Until then the negative abatement cost should not be read as real; blended cement's negative cost (MC-none) is defensible, this one is not.

value-in-db: 0.82, 1.228, and 0.239 t/t, identical to their hosts
issue: The ccs-emissions rule copies the host's gross emissions into the capture variant. The cement kiln with capture therefore shows the same 0.82 t CO2 per t clinker as the kiln without capture while also showing 0.75 t captured, and the lime and glass variants do the same. kiln_oxy-fuel, by contrast, carries a sourced total of 0.088 t/t that is already net of capture, so the two capture routes are not on the same footing.
benchmark: A post-combustion cement kiln retrofit at 90% capture emits about 0.09-0.15 t CO2 per t clinker net; the lime kiln about 0.12-0.2
recommendation: Either net the captured CO2 out of emissions-total for the ccs variants, or state in design.md that emissions-total is gross before capture and make kiln_oxy-fuel consistent with that. A modeller reading wide-archetype today sees no abatement from the ccs archetypes.

value-in-db: fuel 3.28303 GJ/t while coal 2.05426 + natural-gas 1.53769 + oil 0.12375 + petroleum-coke 0.13313 = 3.84883
issue: The ccs-host-plus-addon-energy rule scales the named fuels up by the capture plant's extra duty (coal 1.8066 to 2.0543, a factor of 1.137) but leaves the fuel aggregate at the host value, so the named fuels no longer sum to fuel. The level-1 carriers do not reconcile with the total either (3.283 + 0.729 + 0.242 + 0.278 = 4.53 against a total of 5.453). emissions-combustion is also left at the host's 0.2877 t/t even though the variant burns more fuel.
benchmark: The named fuels must sum to fuel, and the level-1 carriers to the total, as carriers.py sets out
recommendation: Fix the rule to scale fuel and the named fuels together, and to recompute combustion CO2 from the scaled carriers. kiln_lime-rotary-preheater_ccs-diffuse and furnace_regenerative_ccs-diffuse carry the same defect.

issue: Rows are excluded for want of a unit conversion when the unit is only product-qualified: GJ/t-glass, GJ/t-clinker, GJ/t-brick, MWh/t-glass and t-CO2/t-glass. The SPECIES pattern in convert.py admits only CO2 and CH4 species, so t-glass is an unknown atom. This loses the whole zier_2023_001 glass extraction (6 rows, including the 4.4 GJ/t all-electric melting figure and the 4.64-6.58 GJ/t fleet means), the element-energy_2018_001 counterfactual kiln at 3.3 GJ/t clinker, and 0.9 MWh/t-glass for the electric furnace. Separately, three rows in MBtu/short-ton (martin_2000_001 ceramics and glass) are dropped because MBtu is not in the ATOM table, although short-ton is.
benchmark: These units are the archetype's own product unit; 1 MBtu per short ton is 1.1631 GJ/t, and the magnitudes confirm Martin's MBtu means million Btu (4.5 MBtu/short-ton gives 5.2 GJ/t against a pooled 4.47)
recommendation: Register t-glass, t-clinker, t-brick and t-CO2/t-glass as unit aliases (per example in example-conversion.csv, or as a general product-tonne rule), and add MBtu to ATOM at 1.055056 GJ. Then re-pool the glass and ceramic kiln energy values, which currently rest on fewer rows than the sources supply.

archetype: (32 archetypes in these families, e.g. smelting-vessel_flash, calciner_gas-suspension, digester_bayer)
issue: The class-median capacity factor carries a low bound of 0.972603 %. It comes from one example row, tp-mueller_2013_001-0007, where mueller_2013_001's "greater than 355 days per year" was entered as 0.972603 with unit % instead of 97.26 %. The est-class-capacity-factor rule passes it to 157 archetype rows DB-wide, 32 of them mine, and lc-calculated then divides by it: smelting-vessel_flash gets an annual-output low of 1,846 t/yr and a cost-levelized high of 389,239 CAD/t, and leaching-vessel_high-pressure-acid a high of 1.6 million CAD/t.
benchmark: 97.26 % (355/365 days); every levelized high falls by about 100x
recommendation: Fix the one extraction cell to 97.2603 % (or set it as value-min in %), then rebuild; check no other capacity factor is stored as a fraction.

issue: The high comes from tp-etsap_2012_001-0013, which the note itself flags as 15-26 GJ/t expressed PER TONNE OF ALUMINIUM. Only the HHV factor (cf-hhv-lhv-methane) was applied, so 26 GJ/t Al became 28.85 GJ/t alumina. The same basis factor cf-alumina-per-aluminium is correctly applied to the doe_2017_001 and gielen_1997_003 rows in the same pool, so this row was simply missed.
benchmark: 15-26 GJ/t Al divided by 1.93 t alumina/t Al, about 7.8-13.5 GJ/t alumina (8.6-14.9 on HHV)
recommendation: Add cf-alumina-per-aluminium to tp-etsap_2012_001-0013 (and to the paired fuel row that gives the fuel high of 28.33). Related: closed finding R373 fixed the gielen row only.

issue: The fuel carrier (gielen_1997_003, whole Bayer refinery) and the heat carrier (mpp_2023_001 tp-mpp_2023_001-0155, explicitly the 2020 IAI refinery total, digestion plus calcination) are the same quantity entered under two top-level carriers, so the carriers sum to 20.3 GJ/t against a 10.47 total (screen-carriers ratio 1.94). The whole-refinery scope also overlaps calciner_gas-suspension at 3.25 GJ/t, so a model that puts a digester and a calciner in series double counts calcination.
benchmark: Digestion and evaporation alone 7-9 GJ/t alumina; refinery total including calcination 10-11 GJ/t
recommendation: Put the refinery-total rows on one carrier only (heat or fuel, not both), and decide whether digester_bayer is digestion-only or whole-refinery; if whole-refinery, say so in the description so the calciner is not added on top.

issue: All five pooled examples are copper ELECTROWINNING, not leaching: every row carries source-technology electrolysis-cell_copper-electrowinning and schlesinger_2011_001 pp.351, 365-366 (1,800-2,500 kWh/t Cu, cell voltage and current efficiency printed). The heap-leach archetype has therefore taken the tankhouse power, and the emissions-total of 5.8 t CO2e/t (prior finding R658) rides along with it. There is no copper-electrowinning archetype left, which is also why electrolysis-cell_advanced-anodes (1,700 kWh/t, same source pages) is an efficient variant with no conventional base.
benchmark: Heap leaching plus solution handling 0.5-2 GJ/t Cu; copper electrowinning 1,800-2,200 kWh/t Cu (6.5-8 GJ/t)
recommendation: Re-map the five schlesinger electrowinning rows to a copper-electrowinning archetype and make electrolysis-cell_advanced-anodes its efficient variant; leave heap leaching with its own pumping energy.

issue: Carriers are 35x the total (screen-carriers ratio 34.8). The 1.5 GJ/t carrier pair comes from nccp_1999_003 p.151 Table 9-12, printed per tonne of KCl for potash producers and covering drying and crystallization, which reached this archetype when flotation-cell_potash-crystallization was merged away; a froth cell also has no fuel. The total, from nrcan_2005_001 p.49, is per t ore milled while the archetype product unit is t concentrate.
benchmark: Flotation 2-5 kWh/t ore, i.e. 0.2-0.5 GJ/t concentrate at 10-30:1; no fuel carrier
recommendation: Exclude the two potash rows (or return them to a potash archetype), and either convert the nrcan per-t-ore total with an ore-to-concentrate ratio or change the product unit to t ore. Prior findings R651, R652, R653 and S77 touch this archetype; the carriers are still wrong.

issue: The efficient variant uses 32 % more energy than the conventional circuit, the opposite of the archetype description ("about 20 % less"). Within one source, wang_2013_001 p.131 Table 11, the same Huckleberry circuit is 21.5-23.3 kWh/t as SABC and 15.4-21.7 kWh/t with HPGR. The sag-ball central and high both come from a single NRCan gold-milling total (tp-nrcan_2005_002-0030, 13.009 kWh/t, all carriers per t ore), so the high sits below nine of the ten examples, which run to 25.3 kWh/t (0.09108).
benchmark: SAG-ball 15-25 kWh/t ore; HPGR about 20 % below the SAG circuit it replaces
recommendation: Pool the sag-ball electricity from the nine grinding examples rather than the gold-mill total, and derive the HPGR and stirred-mill variants as a saving off the same base. Prior finding R656 is fixed in form (total now equals electricity) but the central moved the wrong way.

issue: The three pooled examples are all etsap_2013_008 desalination rows with source-technology separator_electricity_reverse-osmosis or _electrodialysis; the central is the ETSAP brief's 3.4 kWh/m3 for seawater reverse osmosis. The archetype is lime treatment, settling and polishing of mine water, which has no membrane.
benchmark: Lime treatment, settling and polishing 0.1-0.5 kWh/m3 (0.0004-0.002 GJ/m3)
recommendation: Exclude the desalination rows and re-draft the value, or re-map them to a reverse-osmosis archetype.

issue: The central is the cusano_2017_001 p.648 Table 6.18 row for the RLE route WITH a Waelz kiln (29,380 MJ/t, source-technology electrolysis-cell_zinc_rle-waelz), whose 11,800 MJ/t of coke is the kiln reductant on secondary feed. The straight RLE row in the same table is 15,075 MJ/t with coke 0, and Table 6.8 gives 13.86-20.0 GJ/t. So the archetype reads twice the route it describes and carries a coke carrier an electrowinning cell cannot use.
benchmark: Zinc electrowinning cell 3.0-3.3 MWh/t Zn (11-12 GJ/t); whole roast-leach-electrowin plant about 15 GJ/t
recommendation: Exclude the rle-waelz rows (or split them into a Waelz-kiln archetype) and take the RLE total 15.075 GJ/t with electricity 14.767. Prior finding R388 named the coke; it is still pooled.

issue: Central and high come from doe_2017_001 Appendix A1 rows whose source-technology is press_efficiency-base and press_bat (2,506 and 2,948 Btu/lb), i.e. the Bandwidth study's whole semi-fabrication (extrusion and rolling) intensity, mapped onto a homogenizing furnace. The 12x spread to the 0.5548 low (cusano) is the symptom.
benchmark: Heating aluminium billets to about 580 degC needs 0.4-0.9 GJ/t
recommendation: Exclude or re-map the two doe_2017 press rows and pool only the cusano homogenisation rows. Prior finding R391 recorded the value; this build still shows it and now names the cause.

value-in-db: combustion 1.75 t/t; process 1.54 (prebaked) and 1.83 (soderberg); soderberg total 3.58
issue: Anode-carbon CO2 is counted twice. The etsap_2012_001 1.6-1.9 t/t is the anode consumption emission, already held under emissions-process, but it is also stored as emissions-combustion, and the soderberg emissions-total is built by method 'sum' to 3.58 t CO2/t Al. A cell burns no fuel, so it has no combustion CO2 at all.
benchmark: Direct CO2 from anode consumption 1.5-1.8 t CO2/t Al; total direct including PFC about 1.6-2.0 t CO2e/t Al
recommendation: Drop emissions-combustion on both cells and rebuild emissions-total from process CO2 plus PFC. Prior finding R381 recorded the double count on the prebaked cell; it is still here and now also drives the soderberg total.

issue: Of 28 examples, every directly measured one is excluded for a missing conversion: drebenstedt_2014_001 0.3858-0.5475 L/t, tokac_2025_001 L/min and L/truck-yr, wallace_2021_001 L/h and GJ/h, ahluwalia_2023_001 gal/cycle and gal/t-payload, norgate_2010_001 kg/t ore, intergroup_2017_001 L/kt. What is left to pool is three bcs_2007_001 per-ton-of-material-handled rows spanning 8x (0.01105, 0.05036, 0.08711) plus the NRCan total, so the open basis conflict S89 is really a conversion gap.
benchmark: Drebenstedt's 0.39-0.55 L/t at 38.7 MJ/L is 15-21 MJ/t of material moved, against 11.7 MJ/t in the DB
recommendation: Add diesel volume and mass conversions (L to GJ, kg to GJ) and a payload basis for gal/t-payload, then re-pool; this is the evidence S89 needs.

value-in-db: two rows each: ventilation 0.027216 and a range-only 0.10044-0.199116; pre-reduction 17.5068 and a range-only 25.992-27.792
issue: Each archetype emits two archetype-parameter rows with the same parameter and a blank target, one with a central and one with low and high only. Six such duplicate keys exist DB-wide. Any reader keyed on archetype and parameter takes whichever row it meets first, and the wide view cannot show both.
benchmark: One pooled row per archetype, parameter and target
recommendation: Fix the pooling step to merge a range-only group with the central-bearing group for the same key (or to drop the range-only row once its bounds are in the band).

issue: The pooled heat SEC comes from four kidnay_2019_001 Table 10.3 rows (MEA, DEA, DGA, MDEA, 220-360 kJ/L) whose own extraction notes say the duty is per litre of LEAN AMINE SOLUTION circulated, not per m3 of gas. The pipeline normalised kJ/L straight to GJ/m3 and pooled it as a gas-throughput value, so it is 580x the archetype's own total SEC and it drives cost-levelized calculated-incl-energy to 5.19 CAD/m3 against 0.0018 CAD/m3 for the capital-and-opex levelized cost.
benchmark: Reboiler duty per m3 of raw gas is about 0.0005 GJ/m3: gpsa_2004_001 Example 21-2 prints 13.28 MMBtu/MMscf for 2.8% CO2 and 0.6% H2S, which is 0.00047 GJ/m3 and matches the drafted total of 0.0005 GJ/m3.
recommendation: Exclude the four kidnay_2019_001 kJ/L heat rows for this archetype (they need a circulation rate to be usable) and rebuild the heat carrier from the per-MMscf rows; already open as S92, so close it with this trace rather than re-deriving it.

issue: The rows that are on the right basis were dropped for want of a conversion: gpsa_2004_001 Example 21-2 heat 13.28 MMBtu/MMscf and Example 20-12 heat 280,000 Btu/MMscf are both excluded with "no conversion from Btu/MMscf to GJ/m3", and brandt_2022_001 reboiler fuel 1.25 Btu/Btu is excluded with "no conversion from Btu/Btu to GJ/m3". That leaves the per-litre-of-solution rows (OG001) as the only survivors.
benchmark: 1 MMscf = 28316.8 m3 and 1 Btu = 1.055 kJ; Btu/Btu is a dimensionless duty multiplier that needs the reboiler duty it multiplies.
recommendation: Add a Btu/MMscf to GJ/m3 conversion factor to records/reference/conversion-factor.csv, re-run the normalisation for the gas-treatment-unit archetypes, and leave the Btu/Btu rows excluded with a note that they are a multiplier on duty.

issue: The central is the median of five rows on two different denominators: one element-energy_2021_001 row at 672.4 GBP per t CO2/yr (1500 CAD/t-per-yr) whose capacity of 100 kt/yr is the reference site's TOTAL emissions, not the gas recovered, and four epa_2023_002 rows for well_associated-gas-route-to-sales (a 1-mile 4-inch sales pipeline at a 343.6 t CH4/yr well) normalised per t CH4. The archetype's product is t CO2 from the gas flared, so the EPA rows are on a quantity about 2.75x smaller by mass and from a different device.
benchmark: At 82,000 t CO2/yr of annual output, 3856 CAD/t-per-yr implies CAD 386 million of capital for one flare gas recovery package; element-energy's own reference site is CAD 150 million and a refinery or battery flare gas recovery compressor package is USD 10-30 million.
recommendation: Exclude the epa_2023_002 well_associated-gas-route-to-sales rows from this archetype or re-map them to their own archetype, and confirm with Brad whether element-energy's 100 kt/yr denominator is site emissions or recovered gas. R541 of the 2026-10-04 pass raised the same capex at CAD 150 million; this build is worse.

issue: The central is the median of three pooled values, two of which are two readings of one document (epa_2023_002 Tables 3-11 and 3-19, 6985 and 7719 USD per short ton, single-pollutant cost with no gas credit, and for the generator-powered variant). They outvote the only Canadian VRU source, icf_2015_001 Table 3-8, which gives -4.79 CAD/Mcf with the gas credit and 2.83 CAD/Mcf without, that is -334 to 197 CAD/t-CH4. The pooled co2e target for the same archetype is 45.7 CAD/t-CO2-eq, which is about 1280 CAD/t-CH4 at GWP 28, so the two targets disagree by a factor of 10.
benchmark: VRUs are the cheapest end of the methane curve: negative to about 500 CAD/t-CH4 (ICF 2015, IEA methane abatement model). 13,347 CAD/t-CH4 is more than 20x too high.
recommendation: Keep the two epa_2023_002 rows as one example (they are one source and one generator-powered variant), or move them to a compressor_vapour-recovery_generator-powered archetype, so the median is not set by one document read twice.

issue: All three capex rows come from etsap_2010_012 Table 2 at 4-7.5 USD2006 per GJ/yr, read "by analogy with ETSAP P05" as dollars per GJ/yr of syncrude at 8760 h. On that reading the 2400 MWth plant costs about USD 340 million for roughly 31,000 bbl/d of syncrude. The same table's coal rows are in the same pool as aranda_2014_001's 1220 USD2013/kW, and the two disagree by about 7x, which says the ETSAP capex basis is misread rather than merely low.
benchmark: Built GTL plants are USD 100,000-150,000 per bbl/d of capacity (Oryx about USD 1.6 billion for 34,000 bbl/d, Pearl about USD 19 billion for 140,000 bbl/d), that is roughly 60-100 CAD per GJ/yr, 5-10x the held value. The archetype's levelized cost of 3.21 CAD/GJ, about CAD 19 per bbl before feedstock, is too cheap for the same reason.
recommendation: Re-read ETSAP P06 Table 2's "Capital cost, $/GJ output" against the plant totals the brief prints, or drop the ETSAP capex rows and source GTL capital from a built-plant reference. R559 of the 2026-10-04 pass raised this; it still shows in this build.

issue: Both sourced levelized costs are toro_2021_001 supply costs of DILBIT, built from a discounted cash flow at a 10-12% return and including solvent make-up, diluent, and pipeline transport from Edmonton to Cushing (18.7 CAD/bbl, about 118 CAD/m3 of the 464). They are full-cycle breakeven prices, not plant-gate technology costs, and they sit 3.8x above the pipeline's own cost-levelized calculated for the same archetypes (122 and 112 CAD/m3). A modeller taking cost-levelized would double count transport and the equity return that CIMS applies itself.
benchmark: A plant-gate levelized cost for solvent or electromagnetic in-situ recovery should land near the calculated 110-170 CAD/m3; 464 CAD/m3 is USD 73 per bbl, a WTI-equivalent supply cost.
recommendation: Set these cost-levelized rows aside as supply-cost, or subtract the blending and transport component the source itemises, and ask Brad whether any sourced cost-levelized may include transport and return. The sibling comparison is also broken: well_sagd and well_solvent-assisted have no sourced cost-levelized, so solvent-only looks 3x dearer than SAGD purely from which definition survived.

issue: The carrier target "not-stated" holds compressor SHAFT WORK from zhang_2020_001 Table 15 and pospisil_2019_001 Table 2, which is the same flow already carried as electricity (shaft work divided by 0.95 motor efficiency) or as gas-turbine fuel (shaft work divided by driver efficiency). For liquefaction-train_electric the carriers sum to 2.13 GJ/t against a total of 1.1 GJ/t, almost exactly double. "not-stated" is also not a carrier a modeller can route.
benchmark: Electric-drive liquefaction uses 280-350 kWh per t LNG, which is 1.0-1.3 GJ/t, matching the electricity row alone.
recommendation: Drop the shaft-work rows from the carrier split, or give them a non-carrier target such as shaft-work so they cannot be summed with electricity and fuel. Check the other liquefaction-train archetypes outside this family for the same pattern.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: These three motor archetypes still pool whole-system energy use as motor energy use. motor_induction-standard takes 10 GJ/GJ straight from the US DOE 2016 statement that a compressed-air system has a wire-to-work efficiency of about 10% (doe_2016_002, p.18), and both variants take 13.587 GJ/GJ from a McKane and Hasanbeigi 2010 compressed-air system row (mckane-hasanbeigi_2010_001:compressor_electricity_variable-speed-trim, p.19 Table 5). The product is shaft work, so the value should be 1/motor efficiency. The same source gives 2.08-2.38 GJ/GJ for pumping and fan systems, and the pooler picked the compressed-air row over motor_variable-speed own 2.17 and 2.08 rows. Siblings compressor_electric and motor_premium-efficiency take the inverse identity and read 1.063-1.066, so the family is internally inconsistent by a factor of ten. Already recorded as S85 and R011/R113; this build is worse, not better (the central moved from 2.5 to 10-13.6).
benchmark: 1.04-1.10 GJ/GJ for an IE3 motor at 91-96% efficiency (McCoy and Douglass 2014 Table 4-1, GPSA 2004 Fig. 15-33)
recommendation: Exclude every whole-system row (doe_2016_002 wire-to-work, all mckane-hasanbeigi_2010_001 Table 5 system rows) from the motor archetypes and let the inverse identity set the SEC, or re-scope these as motor-system archetypes per end use and keep the system values. Fixing it also removes the 314 CAD/GJ energy-inclusive levelized cost on motor_variable-speed.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The same US DOE 2016 compressed-air row (doe_2016_002, p.18, efficiency 10%) sits in the motor efficiency pool and sets the pooled low to 10% on motor_induction-standard, which the sibling rule then copies to motor_induction-standard_efficiency-moderate, motor_variable-speed and steam-turbine_drive. The widened highs then exceed 100% (104.19, 106.059, 110.745), which is impossible for a motor or a drive.
benchmark: Standard induction motors 83-95.6%, NEMA Premium 86.5-96.6% (mccoy_2014_001 Tables 4-1 and 4-6, xenergy_1998_001 Table 2-10); the band should be about 80-96%
recommendation: Exclude the doe_2016_002 10% row from the efficiency pool and cap the widened high at 100% for any non-heat-pump efficiency.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The 75% figure these archetypes carry is heat-recovery effectiveness from Galitsky et al. 2008, not a conversion efficiency. The id-sec-from-efficiency identity inverts it into 1.333 GJ of electricity per GJ of space heating delivered, and the single-carrier split makes electricity the only carrier. A heat-recovery ventilator reduces heating demand; its own energy use is fan power. As built, both efficient variants consume more energy per GJ of heat than resistance-heater_space-heating (1.0101) and far more than heat-pump_space (0.2985), so the model would never choose them.
benchmark: Fan and control power on a heat-recovery air handler is about 0.02-0.06 GJ electricity per GJ of heat recovered; the 75% belongs on a recovery-effectiveness parameter, not efficiency
recommendation: Move recovery effectiveness to its own parameter (or a secondary species), block the inverse identity on it, and set these archetypes energy use to fan power with the heat saving expressed against the host heating archetype.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: A guessed SEC of 0.21 GJ/GJ is inverted into a 476% efficiency, which the screen also flags (efficiency-over-100). Free cooling has no COP in the chiller sense and a percentage efficiency above 100 will be read as one. The SEC itself is doubtful too: the guess sets it at 0.7 of heat-pump_space (0.2985), implying free cooling saves only 30% of chiller electricity, when a cooling tower in free-cooling mode runs on tower fan and pump power alone.
benchmark: Free-cooling electricity about 0.03-0.08 GJ per GJ of cooling (COP 12-30); chiller COP 3-6 for comparison
recommendation: Drop the inverse efficiency on this archetype (or give it a COP parameter), and re-draft the SEC at 0.03-0.08 GJ/GJ with a note that it applies only during free-cooling hours.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: Both lighting efficiencies come from the id-efficiency-from-sec inverse rule applied to an SEC that is an index, not an energy ratio: lighting_fluorescent-hid is drafted at 1.0 GJ/GJ as the reference stock and lighting_led-controls at 0.45, so the inverse gives 100% and 222%. The rationale on the rule itself records that it was switched OFF on 2026-09-30 for producing a 7% motor efficiency and a 154% reformer efficiency, yet it is still firing here, and lighting_fluorescent-hid even carries a 142.9% high.
benchmark: Luminous efficacy, not a percentage: HID and fluorescent 60-110 lm/W, LED high-bay 130-170 lm/W (masanet_2012_001 Table 7). No lighting archetype should carry a percentage efficiency.
recommendation: Either confirm the inverse rule is meant to be off and stop it writing these rows, or exclude the lighting (and cooling-tower) archetypes from it and keep efficacy in lm/W as a secondary parameter.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: lighting_fluorescent-hid takes 4 years from Martin et al. 2000 (martin_2000_001, p.150, "estimated average measure life"), which is a lamp-replacement interval, and the sibling rule then gives lighting_led-controls the same 4 years. An LED high bay lasts 50,000-100,000 hours, so this understates its life by three to five times and inverts the economics: the calculated levelized cost comes out at 29.4 CAD/GJ for LED against 14.7 for the incumbent HID. Recorded as R119 in the 2026-10-04 pass at low severity; the propagation to the LED archetype makes it worse than cosmetic.
benchmark: Industrial luminaire or system life 15-20 years; HID or fluorescent lamp 2-5 years at 4,000 h/yr; LED fixture 12-25 years
recommendation: Decide that lighting lifetime is the luminaire (about 15 years for HID and 20 for LED), keep the lamp interval as the component species the archetype already has (2.28 years, n=3), and stop the sibling rule copying a lamp life across lighting technologies.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
archetype: lighting_fluorescent-hid; lighting_led-controls; mobile-equipment_battery-electric; mobile-equipment_diesel; mobile-equipment_diesel-electric; mobile-equipment_spark-ignition; mobile-equipment_hydrogen-fuel-cell (and about 35 others)
issue: Every archetype filled by est-class-capacity-factor takes a low of 0.972603%, which is not a capacity factor but the fraction 355/365 left unscaled. The source row is mueller_2013_001 on fermenter_grain-dry-mill (tp-mueller_2013_001-0007, p.11-17): value 0.972603 with value-min 97.3 in the same row and unit %, derived from "355/365", so the central was never multiplied by 100 while the minimum was. It becomes the minimum of the class pool and then the low on every archetype the rule touches. Divided into the levelized cost it produces the absurd highs of 2,953 CAD/GJ on lighting_fluorescent-hid and 7,322 on lighting_led-controls.
benchmark: The source says "greater than 355 days per year", so 97.3%; class capacity-factor lows should sit around 20-50%
recommendation: Correct the mueller_2013_001 extraction to 97.3% (and add a check that a capacity factor in % never pools below, say, 5), then re-run the fill.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The diesel and the battery-electric figures come from the same source but from different system boundaries. mobile-equipment_diesel takes 27% (normalised 25.65), the tractor average at the PTO and traction split (dea_2026_005, p.10), while mobile-equipment_battery-electric takes 45%, described as "overall system efficiency including motor, pump and hydraulic losses" (dea_2026_005, p.15). The same source gives 12% for diesel on the full hydraulic basis and 85% for the electric driveline, and the archetype also carries 83% as a component species from Kukkonen 2017. Comparing 25.65% with 45% roughly halves the electrification saving, and the sibling rule then spreads a 35.33% median of that mixed pool onto the hybrid and spark-ignition archetypes. The battery-electric central alone was recorded as R120; the boundary mismatch against diesel is the bigger problem.
benchmark: Like for like: diesel 12% and battery-electric 45% at the implement, or diesel 27% and battery-electric 80-85% at the drive. A battery-electric machine should use about a third of the input energy of a diesel one.
recommendation: Pick one boundary for the family (the implement basis reads best for a mobile-work product), tag each dea_2026_005 row with its boundary, and exclude the rows on the other basis.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The band high of 11.4804 GJ/m3 comes from one MIDDEN card, van-geene_2024_001 TC0400 "hydrocracking with hydrogen as fuel" at 12.041 GJ/t, and the 4.32 and 4.10 values that the last pass flagged at 4.5 GJ/t are TC0373 and TC0389. The MIDDEN cards sum every energy input on the card, so the make-up hydrogen (and, on TC0400, the hydrogen fired in the furnaces) is counted as process energy, which no other source in the pool does. 12 GJ per m3 of liquid product is about a third of the product energy content. The high also sets the fuel carrier band to 10.1952 GJ/m3. Recorded as R521 (max then 30.7 GJ/t); the worst row has gone but the basis problem has not.
benchmark: Hydrotreating 0.3-0.6 GJ/m3 and hydrocracking 0.8-2.6 GJ/m3 of feed excluding make-up hydrogen (gary_2007_001 Table 7.4, worrell_2015_001 Table 3, abella_2022_001 PRELIM)
recommendation: Either set the MIDDEN hydrocracking cards aside until the hydrogen input is separated out, or split hydrogen into its own carrier row (the archetype lists hydrogen but has no hydrogen SEC, R523) and keep only the furnace fuel in the total.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: Two separate problems in one pool. First, a wrong basis: giner-santonja_2019_001 (p.612) gives 0.972 kWh per kg of WATER EVAPORATED for a beet-pulp dryer, normalised to 3.4992 GJ/t and pooled as if it were per tonne of product; the identical rule was applied correctly on kiln_lumber-heat-pump, where the matching row is excluded as "ruled out: per t of water evaporated". Second, the carrier split is taken from a single German dairy spray dryer (giner-santonja_2019_001 p.370) whose carriers sum to 8.53 GJ/t, 8.5 times the pooled total, so the wide view shows heat 7.39 and electricity 1.14 against a total of 1.21. The pool also mixes milk and whey powder spray drying (6-7.6 GJ/t of powder) with lactose drying (1.4) and paper drying, hence the 47-fold spread.
benchmark: Per tonne of dried product: paper drying 2.5-4 GJ/t, food spray drying 4-7 GJ/t, lactose and mineral drying 1-2 GJ/t. The water-evaporated rows need a moisture ratio before they can pool.
recommendation: Exclude the per-water-evaporated beet-pulp row, derive the carrier split from the same example set as the total rather than one spray-dryer row, and consider splitting the archetype by duty (paper drying against food and product drying) since the product bases differ.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The efficient variant uses 4.2 times the energy of its own base, which screen-variant.csv flags. Both values are graded sourced, so the variant escaped the 2026-10-05 fix that made efficiency buckets derive from the base archetype (S02-S04). The variant pools four natural-gas-only rows and carries natural gas as its single carrier, while the base pools a much broader and partly mis-based set (see OT010), so the two are not on one basis and the ordering is meaningless.
benchmark: An efficient dryer variant should sit 10-30% below its base, so about 0.85-1.1 GJ/t if the base is right, or the base should be 5-7 GJ/t if the variant pool is the correct basis
recommendation: Settle the base archetype basis first (OT010), then derive this variant from it as a saving rather than pooling it independently.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The single example is epa_2011_001 (pro-103-install-electric-compressors) at USD 6.2 million per year, whose own note reads "incremental operating cost for the five-compressor station". That is mostly the purchased electricity for a whole station, filed as fixed O&M and then divided by one 1,750 hp compressor annual capacity. It is 233 times the family median (1.35) and the cost-ratio back-test predicts 5.1, a ratio of 0.016. It carries straight through to a calculated levelized cost of 413 CAD/GJ (44 times the family median) and 437 CAD/GJ including energy, which double counts the electricity.
benchmark: Non-fuel fixed O&M on an electric compressor drive is 2-6 CAD per GJ/yr of shaft work (about 2-3% of capex, the ratio the fill rule uses)
recommendation: Exclude the epa_2011_001 operating-cost row, or re-tag it as an energy cost and divide it by the five-compressor capacity; then let est-cost-ratio-opex-fixed fill the parameter.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
value-in-db: total 1.65356 GJ/GJ; carriers electricity 0.00874533 and heat 0.141054 only
issue: The carriers account for 9% of the total, as screen-carriers.csv shows (ratio 0.091), because the archetype has no fuel or natural-gas row at all: the natural gas feed and fuel, which is essentially all of an ATR energy input, is missing from the carrier split. The pooled total itself is flagged in the file as disagreeing with the split example. The capture variant does carry fuel at 1.29987, so the two cannot be compared carrier by carrier, and any carrier-based emissions or cost calculation on the base archetype will come out near zero.
benchmark: ATR hydrogen: 1.3-1.6 GJ of natural gas per GJ of hydrogen HHV plus 0.01-0.05 GJ of electricity (nrel_2026_001, Boulamanti and Moya 2017)
recommendation: Add the natural-gas and fuel carrier rows from the same examples that set the total (or split the total 95/5 gas to electricity as the capture variant does), and resolve the flagged disagreement between the total and the split example.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: Five unrelated archetypes carry the identical abatement cost and the identical band, every one of them an est-range-midpoint of one doe_2023_001 row (p.103, App. B). The source prints a bucket range for energy-efficiency measures rather than a technology-specific cost, so the value says nothing about a variable-speed drive in particular. The DOE figure is also after US Inflation Reduction Act incentives at a 10% WACC for 2030, which does not transfer to a Canadian cost of abatement. A negative cost on a VSD is credible in a MACC, but not this number on these five technologies.
benchmark: A Canadian VSD retrofit at 2025 industrial power prices lands roughly -40 to -120 CAD/t, but it should be computed from this build own capex, SEC saving, and energy price rather than copied from a US bucket
recommendation: Treat the doe_2023_001 App. B ranges as a sector bucket, not a per-technology value: either set them aside or tag them clearly as a US post-IRA MACC bucket, and compute abatement cost inside the build from capex, SEC, and the reference energy prices.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
archetype: melting-furnace_induction; refinery_sugar-beet; preheater_ladle; fan_mine-ventilation; smelting-vessel_smelting-reduction; process-improvement_pre-reduction
value-in-db: two rows per archetype for the same parameter and target
issue: Six archetypes have two rows in archetype-parameter.csv for the same (archetype, specific-energy-consumption, blank target). On melting-furnace_induction one row is a range-only row (blank central, 2.16-4.32 GJ/t) and the other a central of 3.6 with no band; the wide view picked 3.6 and lost the band. A duplicate key means any consumer reading the long table keyed on archetype and parameter gets whichever row comes last.
benchmark: One pooled row per archetype, parameter, and target
recommendation: Merge range-only rows into the pooled row (use them to set low and high where the central comes from elsewhere) so the key stays unique, and add a build check that the key is unique.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
value-in-db: 7.38993 GJ/t against a total of 3.31933 and fuel of 3.13573
issue: The named fuel exceeds both the aggregate fuel row and the archetype total by more than twice. The total and the fuel share come from Aries et al. 2024 (SF BREF), while the natural-gas row is an est-range-midpoint from a different example, so it was never reconciled with the split it belongs to. Since natural gas is the only fuel this furnace burns, it should equal the fuel row.
benchmark: Steel heat-treatment and annealing furnaces 1.5-4 GJ/t of product; natural gas should equal the fuel row at about 3.1 GJ/t
recommendation: Derive the natural-gas row as 100% of the fuel row (the single-carrier-split identity other archetypes use) instead of pooling a separate range midpoint.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
archetype: management-system_leak-detection (and any other archetype whose source prints "y")
issue: The 2-year lifetime is a pool of EPA repair lives and time horizons (epa_2006_001 "repair life assumed to be 2 years", epa_2019_001 "time horizon" of 1 year) together with IEA project lives of 5 and 10 years. Meanwhile eleven nccp_1999_005 rows that print a 20 or 25 year project life are all excluded with "no conversion from y to years", so the unit string "y" is not recognised as an alias of years. The archetype is outside my families (oil-and-gas), but the missing alias is cross-cutting and the lifetime it produces drives every levelized cost on the archetype.
benchmark: An LDAR programme has no equipment lifetime in the capital-stock sense; the IEA project life of 5-10 years is the usable convention, and the NCCP 20-25 year rows should at least be visible
recommendation: Add "y" (and "yr", "yrs") as aliases of years in records/reference/unit-conversion.csv, then decide whether repair-life and time-horizon rows belong in the lifetime pool at all or need a species of their own.

issue: The rule inverts a specific energy consumption that counts only utilities. Both archetypes list carriers of steam and electricity only, so the pooled SEC (0.2017 GJ/GJ from Zhang et al. 2003 part 1, record tp-zhang_2003_002 via example zhang_2003_002:transesterification-unit_acid-catalyzed@process-iii; 0.2135 GJ/GJ from West et al. 2008, west_2008_001:transesterification-unit_supercritical-methanol@process-iv) excludes the oil feedstock and the methanol. The rule's require-consistent-total guard passes because the total equals the single named carrier, which proves nothing about whether the feedstock is counted.
benchmark: A transesterification unit converts 88-92 % of the feed oil energy into FAME. The sibling transesterification-unit_alkali-catalyzed holds 90.3 % sourced from DEA 2026, and the heterogeneous-catalyst sibling takes 90.3 % from it. Nothing that makes a fuel can exceed 100 %.
recommendation: Add a condition to id-efficiency-from-sec in records/fill/fill-rule.csv: fire only where the carrier split includes the archetype's feedstock carrier (bioliquid, biomass, biogas, syngas or similar), and drop the plausible ceiling from 800 % to about 105 % except on heat-pump equipment. In the meantime take 90.3 % from the alkali-catalyzed sibling, as est-sibling-efficiency already does for the heterogeneous-catalyst unit.

issue: Four Mueller and Kwik 2013 rows (tp-mueller_2013_001-0007, -0010, -0013, -0016) record 'greater than 355 days per year' as 0.972603 in a per-cent field: the fraction 355/365 was never multiplied by 100. The low band then travels out through est-class-capacity-factor and est-sibling-capacity-factor to 157 archetypes in 17 families, including digester_continuous-kraft, paper-machine, pulper_thermomechanical, blast-furnace and every mobile-equipment archetype, all of which now carry a capacity-factor low of 0.97 %.
benchmark: 97.26 % (355 days of 365). The previous pass recorded this as R182 at medium severity and it still shows in this build; the propagation makes it the most consequential single cell in the database.
recommendation: Correct the four Mueller and Kwik rows to 97.26 % (or record the days and let the pipeline divide), and add a bound check that rejects a capacity-factor below about 10 % in per cent. Re-run: 157 archetypes' bands and every levelized cost that uses them change.

value-in-db: 1.112 t/t black liquor solids (n=4, IEAGHG 2016 and Kuparinen et al. 2019)
issue: Every example behind this value is biogenic CO2 and says so. IEAGHG's row (tp-ieaghg_2016_001-0052) is noted '2053 kg CO2/adt, all biogenic'; Kuparinen's rows (tp-kuparinen_2019_001-0001, -0004, -0011) say 'Biogenic CO2 from black liquor combustion'. design.md line 549 and the 2026-10-10 ruling in decisions.md both put biogenic CO2 in CIMS's emissions-biomass, not emissions-combustion. Every other biomass-fired pulp archetype correctly gets 0 from zero-if-no-fossil, so the recovery boiler is the one archetype reporting biogenic carbon as though it were fossil, and it is the largest CO2 number in a kraft mill.
benchmark: Fossil combustion CO2 on a recovery boiler firing only black liquor is 0 t/t BLS; the 1.11 t/t belongs in emissions-biomass.
recommendation: Move the four black-liquor rows to emissions-biomass (or add the parameter if it is not yet in the schema) and leave emissions-combustion at 0. The sibling boiler_recovery-high-solids has no CO2 row at all, so fix both together.

value-in-db: 0.58235 t/t lime (n=4, IEAGHG 2016 and Kuparinen et al. 2019)
issue: The calcination CO2 in a kraft lime kiln comes from lime mud made in the causticizing cycle from wood-derived carbon, and all four sources label it biogenic: tp-ieaghg_2016_001-0058 'calcination CO2 ... classed biogenic', tp-ieaghg_2016_001-0062 'calcination (biogenic per the source)', tp-kuparinen_2019_001-0008 and -0015 'biogenic share 64 % / 55 % (lime reburning reaction)'. It sits in emissions-process alongside genuinely fossil process CO2 elsewhere in the database. The companion emissions-combustion value of 0.4058 t/t is correctly the fossil heavy fuel oil and gas part.
benchmark: Process CO2 from kraft lime reburning is biogenic, so 0 fossil; the cement and lime families' 0.785 t CO2 per t CaO from limestone is the fossil-equivalent case and should not share a field with it.
recommendation: Move the kraft lime-kiln calcination rows to emissions-biomass and keep emissions-process for mineral-carbonate CO2, or add a biogenic flag column to the emissions rows. Note the same split on kiln_lime-rotary_efficiency-strong, whose 0.2945 t/t comes from the fuel-emission-factor identity.

value-in-db: capacity 102.2 kt/yr; capex 448.887 2025_CAD/t-per-yr; opex-fixed 64.3735; SEC 26.5 GJ/t
issue: Every example is per tonne of extracted lignin, but archetype.csv declares the product as black liquor solids in tonnes. Kuparinen et al. 2017 (tp-kuparinen_2017_001-0006) gives 280 t/d of 'lignin production' and Tomani 2010 (tp-tomani_2010_001-0001) 50,000 t/yr 'of lignin, calculated as dry product'. The SEC guess note already doubts the unit and says to divide by about 6 if the unit is total black liquor solids. A 102 kt/yr capacity also makes no sense beside its declared siblings boiler_recovery and evaporator_multiple-effect at 2,470 kt/yr of BLS.
benchmark: A lignin plant removes roughly 0.15-0.25 t lignin per t BLS, so on a per-t-BLS basis the capex would be about 70-110 CAD/t-per-yr and the energy 4-6 GJ/t, not 449 and 26.5.
recommendation: Either change the archetype's product and product-unit to lignin in tonnes, which is what every source states, or add a lignin-per-BLS conversion factor and apply it to capacity, capex, opex and the SEC. Ask Brad which basis CIMS wants, since the archetype's flows connect to the recovery cycle.

issue: The pool mixes three bases. Kuparinen et al. 2019 (tp-kuparinen_2019_001-0010) gives 6,768 t/d of black liquor dry solids, which becomes 2,470 kt/yr and sets the central value; IEAGHG 2016 (tp-ieaghg_2016_001-0053) gives 4,985 t/d with capacity-basis product-output, 't of pulp', which becomes 3,384 kt/yr; Suhr et al. 2015 (tp-suhr_2015_001-0036) gives 1,500 ADt/d of pulp as 821 kt/yr; and IETD (tp-ietd_2013_001-0154) gives 150 t/h of boiler steam as 1,314 kt/yr. The per-ADt-pulp and the steam capacities never get the solids ratio that the same pipeline applies to the energy rows, and separately Lipiainen et al. 2022's two rows in tds/d (2,621 and 1,627) are dropped for 'no conversion from tds/d to kt/yr' even though Vakkilainen's identical t/d rows convert.
benchmark: The largest recovery boilers ever built fire about 5,000-5,800 t BLS/d, i.e. 1,800-2,100 kt BLS/yr; Vakkilainen's 3,000 t/d example at 1,095 kt/yr is a normal large unit. A central of 2,470 kt/yr is above the world's biggest boiler.
recommendation: Apply each source's solids ratio to the per-ADt-pulp capacities (IEAGHG 1.86, Suhr the generic 1.5), exclude the IETD steam-capacity row or re-base it on thermal output, and add tds/d as an alias of t/d in the unit table so the Lipiainen fleet averages pool.

issue: The only example (tp-larson_2006_001-0002) is 548,277 bone-dry short tons per year of the reference mill's total pulp production, converted straight to tonnes and pooled on an archetype whose product is black liquor solids. Nothing applies the solids ratio or the oven-dry to air-dry step. It is also inconsistent with the archetype's own capacity and capacity factor: 2,470 kt/yr at 95.09 % would be about 2,348 kt/yr, 4.7 times the stated annual output. The levelized cost per tonne in wide-archetype.csv rests on this number.
benchmark: On the mill Larson describes, black liquor solids would be roughly 1.5 x 497 kt of oven-dry pulp, so about 830 kt BLS/yr once the ODt to ADt step is taken too.
recommendation: Re-base the row with cf-bls-per-pulp and the oven-dry step, or exclude it and let the capacity x capacity-factor identity set annual output. Add a pipeline check that annual-output agrees with capacity x capacity-factor within a factor of about 1.3.

issue: Martin et al. 2000 (emerging technologies) states its fuel rows in MBtu/short-ton and all seven are dropped with 'no conversion from MBtu/short-ton to GJ/t' (tp-martin_2000_001-0021, -0025, -0032, -0042, -0046, -0053, -0067), while the identical quantity spelled MMBtu/ton from US DOE 2015 converts without trouble.
