These are exactly the reference-versus-new-measure pairs that would discipline the totals flagged in PB012 and PB014.
benchmark: 1 MMBtu/short ton = 1.1631 GJ/t, the same factor the pipeline already uses for MMBtu/ton.
recommendation: Add MBtu/short-ton, MBtu/ton and MMBtu/short-ton as aliases of MMBtu/ton in the unit table, then re-run and re-read the affected archetypes.

value-in-db: total 0.00312244 GJ/GJ against a carrier sum of 1.3315
issue: The pooled total comes from Van Geene et al. 2024 (MIDDEN) and the carrier split from DEA 2026 (dea_2026_003:reactor_hvo-renewable-diesel@104-hvo-renewable-diesel). They differ by a factor of 426, which screen-carriers.csv flags, and the pipeline left the carriers unscaled. The DEA split (bioliquid 1.036, hydrogen 0.139, natural gas 0.009) is a full HEFA energy balance including the feed oil; the MIDDEN figure of 0.0031 GJ/GJ is too small to be even the electricity of a hydrotreater.
benchmark: A HEFA unit consumes about 1.03-1.08 GJ of feed oil plus 0.08-0.15 GJ of hydrogen and 0.01-0.03 GJ of utilities per GJ of product, i.e. a total near 1.2 GJ/GJ, consistent with the archetype's sourced efficiency of 66 %.
recommendation: Exclude or re-read the MIDDEN total (tp-van-geene_2024_001 row for this archetype) and let the DEA carrier sum set the total. The same MIDDEN-against-DEA clash drives PB011 and PB012, so check all three together.

value-in-db: total 0.0463483 GJ/GJ against a carrier sum of 1.2662
issue: Same pattern as PB010: the total is Van Geene et al. 2024 (MIDDEN) and the split is DEA 2026 (dea_2026_003:transesterification-unit_vegetable-oil@101-fame-biodiesel-veg-oil), 27 times apart, and the rationale admits one of the two is on another scope. The archetype's carriers list holds only electricity even though the pooled rows include bioliquid 1.024, methanol 0.055, natural gas 0.029, heat 0.058 and steam 0.096.
benchmark: A FAME plant uses about 1.02-1.05 GJ of oil, 0.05-0.06 GJ of methanol and 0.03-0.10 GJ of utilities per GJ of biodiesel, which matches the DEA split and the archetype's sourced 90.3 % efficiency.
recommendation: Take the DEA carrier sum as the total, and extend the carriers list to bioliquid, methanol, natural gas and steam. This also removes the premise failure behind PB001 for the two siblings.

value-in-db: total 0.104 GJ/t against an electricity carrier of 0.9 GJ/t
issue: The total is Van Geene et al. 2024 (MIDDEN) and the only carrier is Suhr et al. 2015 PP BREF (suhr_2015_001:dryer_heat-pump@heat-recovery-with-heat-pumps-sect-7-4-3-emerging), 8.7 times apart, carriers left unscaled. 0.104 GJ/t of dried product cannot dry anything: the conventional siblings dryer_market-pulp and dryer_steam-heated need 2.68 and 4.02 GJ/t.
benchmark: 0.9 GJ/t of electricity at the archetype's own sourced COP of 300 % delivers 2.7 GJ/t of drying heat, which lines up with the conventional dryers. The 0.9 GJ/t carrier is the right number and the total is wrong.
recommendation: Exclude or re-read the MIDDEN total and set the total to the electricity carrier of 0.9 GJ/t. The archetype's 300 % efficiency is a COP and is legitimate, but it is the only >100 % value in the family that is, so keep it exempt from any efficiency bound you add for PB001.

value-in-db: 3748.44, 3756.84 and 3909.59 2025_CAD/t-per-yr against a paper-forming group median of 691.849
issue: Bataille et al. 2017 prices a whole paper machine, but the archetype is defined in archetype.csv as the forming and press sections, with drying split out to dryer_steam-heated. The capital of the dryer section is therefore counted twice when a mill is built from these archetypes. It is the same scope mismatch that S96 records on the energy side (total 6.7 GJ/t against a carrier sum of 2.36), and S96 is still open in this build, so the archetype is consistently carrying whole-machine numbers on both cost and energy while the design says forming and press.
benchmark: A complete paper machine runs about 3,000-4,000 CAD per annual tonne, which is what 3,748 represents. The forming and press sections are roughly 40-50 % of that, so about 1,500-1,900 CAD/t-per-yr, and the sibling press_shoe-extended's 72 CAD/t-per-yr shows what a press-only number looks like.
recommendation: Decide the archetype's scope once and apply it to both parameters: either widen paper-machine to the whole machine and stop pairing it with a separate dryer, or split Bataille's capex and the 6.7 GJ/t total between the forming-press and drying archetypes. Record it against S96 rather than as a separate item.

value-in-db: high bands of 55,913, 52,297, 50,276 and 4,428 2025_CAD/t against centrals of 516, 538, 517 and 319
issue: The levelized calculation divides by the low end of capacity factor and annual output, so the 0.9726 % capacity-factor low from PB002 turns into a cost high two orders of magnitude above the central. paper-machine_waterless compounds it with an annual-output low of 243 t/yr against a central of 22,500, from est-end-use-annual-output on a group of one. A band from 72 to 55,913 CAD/t tells a modeller nothing.
benchmark: A band of roughly 0.5x to 2x the central, so about 250-1,000 CAD/t for a paper machine.
recommendation: Fix PB002 first, then clamp the levelized band: carry the central's own capacity factor into the band or floor the divisor at a sane capacity factor, and do not let an end-use median built from a single archetype set an annual-output low.

issue: The variant sits at 13 % of its base, fermenter_grain-dry-mill at 0.364226 GJ/GJ, so a moderate efficiency measure appears to cut energy use by 87 %. The total comes from Galitsky et al. 2003 on corn wet milling, a different process from the dry mill this variant modifies, and the two carrier rows are savings-sized rather than consumption-sized: an electricity figure of 1.0e-06 GJ/GJ is a microjoule per gigajoule.
benchmark: A moderate efficiency package on a grain dry mill saves 5-15 %, so the variant should sit around 0.31-0.35 GJ/GJ, just below its base.
recommendation: Re-read the Galitsky rows: if they are savings, not consumption, they belong in the bucket-saving path, not in specific-energy-consumption. Then let the variant take its base less the saving. Check the wet-mill source against the dry-mill archetype at the same time.

value-in-db: coal 0.116039 GJ/t and not-stated 0.130061 on boiler_recovery_ccs-diffuse; four zero carriers on each biofuels variant
issue: The ccs-host-plus-addon-energy rule splits the capture plant's energy by the mean carrier shares of the whole CO2-capture node, so it stamps iron-and-steel and coal carriers onto a kraft recovery boiler and an ethanol plant. A recovery boiler with capture now burns 0.116 GJ/t of coal and 0.130 GJ/t of 'not-stated', and the biofuels variants carry blast-furnace gas, coke-oven gas and by-product gas rows at zero. S101 records the zero rows on fermenter_grain-dry-mill and is still open; the non-zero coal on boiler_recovery_ccs-diffuse is the worse half and is not yet recorded.
benchmark: Capture on a kraft recovery boiler draws steam and electricity from the mill, so the add-on should carry only steam, electricity and perhaps natural gas.
recommendation: Restrict the carrier split to carriers the host archetype actually lists, or to the capture archetypes that share the host's sector, and drop zero rows rather than publishing them. Extend S101 to cover boiler_recovery_ccs-diffuse.

issue: This capture variant carries no share-to-capture row at all, while every other concentrated-capture archetype in the family has one, so the CIMS capture node has no rate to read. Its emissions-captured of 1.8 t/t is a judgement guess and exceeds the host's process CO2 of 1.72 t/t. The archetype also still carries ammonia as an input carrier set to zero, which is open item S94.
benchmark: An ATR ammonia plant sends roughly 85-95% of its CO2 through the shift and acid-gas removal, so a share of about 85-90% and captured of about 1.8-2.0 t/t is defensible; the number just needs to be recorded.
recommendation: Write a share-to-capture row for this archetype (derive it from the guessed captured value as the SMR sibling does) and drop the ammonia carrier under S94.

issue: The total (van-geene_2024_001 TC0431 and TC0437, where furnace emissions are avoided) is nine times smaller than the combustion value (purola_2021_001 and mynko_2023_001, which keep a gas-fired feed preheater). Total below combustion is impossible, and the two example sets describe different designs: a fully electrified cracker and one with a fired preheater.
benchmark: An electrified cracker that keeps a gas preheater emits roughly 0.05-0.10 t CO2/t; one with an electric preheater and exported off-gas approaches zero. Pick the design, then the total must be at least the combustion value.
recommendation: Split the archetype by preheater design, or keep one design and exclude the other source's rows so total is greater than or equal to combustion.

issue: A COP-like efficiency of 8.8 is recorded for an archetype whose carriers are steam and natural gas with no electricity, so nothing in the archetype can deliver the work the COP implies. All six examples are kiss_2012_001. The previous pass recorded this as R404 and the build still shows it, now higher (883% against the earlier 9.8).
benchmark: Heat-integrated or internally heat-integrated columns save 30-60% of reboiler duty; their thermal efficiency is below 100%. A COP of 5-10 belongs to the heat-pumped archetype, which already carries 525%.
recommendation: Move the Kiss COP rows to distillation-column_heat-pumped or record them as an energy-saving ratio, not an efficiency. See R404.

issue: The co2e row (median of 4) does not follow from the n2o row on the same archetype: 0.0085 t N2O/t is 2.25-2.53 t CO2e/t at GWP 265-298. A nitric acid plant has no process CO2, so the two should agree. R453 in the previous pass; still present.
benchmark: 2.25-2.53 t CO2e/t for the 8.5 kg N2O/t central, or about 0.5-1.5 t CO2e/t if the archetype is meant to be a partly abated plant.
recommendation: Compute emissions-process co2e from the n2o central and the GWP, and drop the mixed abated and unabated co2e examples. See R453.

issue: All four examples are IEA 2013 fence-to-fence intensities excluding feedstock energy (0.57, 0.75, 1 and 2 GJ/t), and the median of 0.875 GJ/t sits below the endothermic heat of ethanol dehydration alone. The archetype also lists no carriers and no ethanol feed ratio, so the model sees a near-free conversion step.
benchmark: Ethanol dehydration needs about 1.6 GJ/t ethylene of reaction enthalpy before separation losses; reported plant heat demand is 2-6 GJ/t ethylene. The 2 GJ/t Ren and DECHEMA value is the defensible floor.
recommendation: Take the 2 GJ/t DECHEMA value as the central, add the ethanol feed ratio (about 1.7 t/t) as a flow, and give the archetype a carrier list.

issue: The archetype has no specific-energy-consumption central at all, sourced or filled, although it has seven examples and a capex of 3050 CAD/t-yr, so a model run cannot price its energy. Its variable O&M of 3655 CAD/t is 65x the family median and most likely carries the hydrogen and CO2 feedstock. R208 in the previous pass listed the reactor_co2-to-* archetypes as carrying no usable central; this one still does not.
benchmark: CO2-to-OME3-5 needs roughly 1.5-1.9 t CO2 and 0.25-0.35 t H2 per t product, that is about 35-50 GJ/t of hydrogen input; non-feedstock O&M is of the order of 100-300 CAD/t.
recommendation: Fill the SEC from the hydrogen and electricity stoichiometry, and split the feedstock out of opex-variable so the model does not price hydrogen twice.

issue: Capex is 7.1x the family median on one sourced example, and the fixed O&M that the cost-ratio rule derives from it is 6.6x the median. R419 in the previous pass put it at roughly 2x the literature; the build still shows the same value.
benchmark: Biomass gasification to ammonia is about 2500-4000 USD per kW of hydrogen, that is roughly 2600-4400 CAD per t NH3 per year plus about 600 for the synthesis loop, so about 3000-5000 CAD/t-yr.
recommendation: Re-read the source for scope (it probably includes feedstock handling or a first-of-a-kind premium) and widen or lower the central. See R419.

issue: Capex is a tenth of the family median on three sourced examples. R452 in the previous pass judged it 2-3x low and the build still shows it.
benchmark: A 330 kt/yr dual-pressure nitric acid plant cost 60-100 M EUR in 2007, that is roughly 300-600 CAD per t-yr in 2025 money.
recommendation: Re-check the three examples for a retrofit or unit scope, and note that two incremental rows are set aside under open item S59.

value-in-db: SEC 12.08 GJ/t; lifetime 5 years; capex 1621 CAD/t-per-yr
issue: The moderate efficiency variant sits 40% below its base archetype (20.31 GJ/t) for a measure set whose own emissions-reduction-potential is 10%, its life of 5 years is a payback or catalyst interval rather than a measure life (the sibling back-test misses it by 5x), and its capex is 93% of a whole new cracker. R477, R478 and R479 in the previous pass; all three still show.
benchmark: A 10% measure set on a 20.3 GJ/t cracker should give about 18 GJ/t, a measure life of 10-20 years, and an incremental capex well below the host's 1744 CAD/t-yr.
recommendation: Derive the variant's SEC from the base and its own 10% potential, replace the 5-year life, and make capex an increment. See R477 to R479.

issue: The four DEA 2026 values are heat-pump COPs for geothermal district-heating plants with an electric or absorption heat pump, not an efficiency of the well. The inverse identity has now carried them into SEC [geothermal] 0.267 GJ/GJ, so the model draws 0.27 GJ of geothermal heat per GJ delivered and pays nothing for the pump electricity.
benchmark: Direct geothermal use: pump power 2-5 % of the heat delivered, so SEC [electricity] about 0.02-0.05 GJ/GJ and SEC [geothermal] about 1.0 GJ/GJ.
recommendation: Move the DEA COP rows to a heat-pump-assisted archetype or drop the efficiency, and set SEC [geothermal] to about 1.0 with a separate pump-electricity row. R067 raised this on geothermal-well_enhanced; this build shows it on geothermal-well_direct-use and the identity has spread it.

issue: The band's high is tp-concawe_2019_001-0025, 8.1 GJ per tonne of CO2 avoided, pooled into a parameter whose denominator is CO2 captured everywhere else. The low, tp-iea_2021_001-0019, is a dilute ammonia-plant flue-gas case. Mixing avoided and captured denominators widens the band by roughly 20-40 %.
benchmark: MEA on dilute flue gas: 3.5-4.5 GJ/t CO2 captured on a primary-fuel basis, or 3.2-3.8 GJ/t as reboiler steam.
recommendation: Convert the Concawe row to a per-t-captured basis using its own capture rate, or exclude it and note the avoided basis.

value-in-db: amine carriers sum to 11.4915 GJ/t against a total of 4.87835 (screen-carriers ratio 2.36)
issue: Across the capture family and the fossil heat-supply archetypes, fuel is a roll-up of the named fossil carriers (boiler_oxy-fuel: fuel 1.21245 = coal 0.995013 + natural-gas 0.217437), and heat and steam are two names for one reboiler duty (amine heat 3.4205, steam 3.19264). Any sum over carriers therefore double- or triple-counts. wide-archetype.csv exposes only the untagged total, but wide-archetype-carriers-species.csv lists them side by side with nothing marking which are alternatives.
benchmark: One reboiler duty per archetype: amine 3.2-3.8 GJ/t as steam, or 4.0-4.5 GJ/t as the gas burned to raise it, never both.
recommendation: Mark each carrier row as additive or alternative in the carriers view (a basis column), or collapse heat into steam and drop the fuel roll-up where named carriers exist, so the carriers view can be summed safely.

value-in-db: efficiency 72.015 % (inverse on the as-sourced SEC 1.3886) against primary SEC 1.76845 GJ/GJ
issue: The efficiency is inverted from the as-sourced secondary SEC (1.3886 GJ/GJ, nrel_2026_001), while the primary SEC is the ccs-energy build-up (host 1.65356 plus add-on 0.114888 = 1.76845). A modeller using efficiency gets 1.39 GJ/GJ, one using SEC gets 1.77, a 27 % gap on one archetype. gasifier_coal-petroleum-coke_ccs-concentrated shows the same split (efficiency 63.78 % = 1.57 against SEC 1.99456).
benchmark: The two should be one quantity: for an ATR with capture, 1.5-1.7 GJ natural gas per GJ H2 HHV including the capture penalty.
recommendation: Derive efficiency from the same SEC the archetype publishes (the ccs-energy total), or publish the as-sourced SEC as the primary so the pair closes.

value-in-db: natural-gas 1.51915 GJ/GJ against fuel 1.429 GJ/GJ, both estimated by ccs-energy
issue: The named carrier exceeds its own roll-up, so the ccs-energy rule built the two from different host rows. The same archetype also carries coal 0.0701816 and a not-stated carrier 0.0786618, neither of which can be right for a gas boiler with capture, and its efficiency band runs 56.87 % to 95 % for one device.
benchmark: A gas boiler with post-combustion capture: about 1.5-1.9 GJ gas per GJ of steam delivered, with fuel equal to the sum of the named fossil carriers.
recommendation: Make the ccs-energy rule build fuel as the sum of the named carriers it writes, and drop the coal and not-stated rows on a gas host.

value-in-db: 5 GJ/t (n=1, element-energy_2021_001) against the archetype's own steam 2.35 and total 2.08032 GJ/t
issue: The heat row is more than twice the archetype's own steam row and total, and higher than the amine archetype it is meant to undercut. Three statements of one duty disagree by 2.4x inside one archetype.
benchmark: Chemical-solvent capture on a concentrated stream: 1.5-2.5 GJ/t CO2; MEA on flue gas 3.2-4.0 GJ/t.
recommendation: Re-read the Element Energy locator (it may be per t of CO2 avoided, or a flue-gas case) and reconcile heat with steam. Still present from R141 of the 2026-10-04 pass.

issue: The species rests on one 2004 BC Hydro EPRI TAG row (tp-bc-hydro_2004_001-0095) whose note reads: fuel cell project life estimates 2000 to 10,000 hours; developers aim for 5 years. Those are early-demonstration stack figures, and they now sit 6.7x below the stack species on the same archetype (4.56621 years, 40,000 h, ETSAP E12).
benchmark: Modern fuel-cell stack life 40,000-90,000 h (ETSAP E12, DEA 2026); system life 10-20 years, which the primary lifetime already gives as 10.
recommendation: Exclude the 2004 BC Hydro row, or fold it into the stack species as its low bound; a component species 6.7x below the stack species is not usable.

value-in-db: capex 260 2025_CAD/GJ-per-yr, grade guess, method judgement, no sources
issue: The archetype has 36 examples and 21 sourced capacity values, yet its whole cost stack is a judgement guess with no source listed, and cost-levelized [calculated] 51.67 CAD/GJ inherits that grade. The sibling reactor_small-nuclear-power is the same plant on an electricity basis and should constrain it.
benchmark: SMR overnight cost 6,000-12,000 USD/kWe; on a thermal basis at a 90 % capacity factor, roughly 80-250 CAD/GJ-yr.
recommendation: Pull a capex from the sourced SMR examples (nrel_2016_001, abou-jaoude_2024_001), or derive it from reactor_small-nuclear-power's capex and the thermal-to-electric ratio, so the heat archetype is not a bare guess.

issue: The guessed capex, with lifetime 50 years and the fill's capital recovery, produces cost-levelized [calculated] 21.4665 CAD/t, three times the archetype's own sourced levelized cost of 7.17 CAD/t (etsap_2010_007). Two cost answers on one archetype differ by 3x.
benchmark: Onshore CO2 trunk pipeline 2-15 CAD/t transported (IEAGHG, ETSAP E17); a capex consistent with that is roughly 40-60 CAD/t-per-yr.
recommendation: Back the capex out of the sourced levelized cost rather than guessing it, or mark the guess as subordinate so the identity does not override a sourced number. R153 noted this archetype had no capex at all.

value-in-db: efficiency 80 % (guess, inverse), SEC 1.25 GJ/GJ (guess, judgement), capex 7 2025_CAD/GJ-per-yr (guess)
issue: The archetype has 9 examples but every parameter that matters is a guess, and the guesses are circular: the efficiency is the inverse of the guessed SEC. Meanwhile set-aside-efficiency.csv sets aside a real sourced capex (tp-nedo_2008_001-0013, 7,167 JPY/kW) with the reason that neither the example nor the archetype has an efficiency, although the archetype does carry one, just a guessed one.
benchmark: Flue-gas heat recovery (economiser, recuperator): 60-85 % of the recoverable heat delivered; capex 10-40 CAD/GJ-yr.
recommendation: Either let the bridge use a guessed efficiency and recover the NEDO capex, or say in the set-aside reason that only sourced efficiencies bridge; and source an efficiency for this archetype from the 9 examples.

value-in-db: liquefaction-train 11.544 CAD/GJ with a high of 1849.62 (160x the central); adsorber_pressure-swing 28.16 with a high of 1345.06
issue: The levelized identity compounds the extremes of capex, capacity factor, lifetime, and energy, so the high band multiplies several worst cases at once. A high of 1,850 CAD/GJ is 265 CAD per kg of hydrogen. Thirty rows in these four families have a high at least 8x the central.
benchmark: A usable band on a levelized cost is roughly 0.5x to 3x the central; the inputs' own bands do not justify 100x.
recommendation: Propagate the band by combining input percentiles (for instance low capex with the central capacity factor) rather than corner to corner, or publish the band only where every input has one.

value-in-db: biomass 2.59 GJ/GJ and municipal-waste 1.11 GJ/GJ, both grade guess, method judgement
issue: The two feedstock carriers are alternatives for one digester, not two inputs, yet both are written at full value, so the carriers sum to 3.70 GJ of feedstock per GJ of heat. There is no sourced SEC on the archetype to anchor either.
benchmark: Biogas CHP delivering heat as the product: 2.0-2.5 GJ of feedstock per GJ of heat, with electricity as a by-product.
recommendation: Write the two feedstock carriers as shares of one total, as the ccs-energy rule does, or keep only the dominant carrier.

issue: The same gross-versus-net mixing one level up. The pool is doe_2015_001 0.67 (gross), van-geene_2024_001 0.1787, golder_2021_001 0.284 (the note says net), and pardo_2013_001 -0.853 (net of recovery), so the sign flip inside the band is a scope difference, not a spread.
benchmark: BOF without gas recovery +0.3 to +0.7 GJ/t; with full recovery -0.5 to -0.8 GJ/t (IS BREF 2013)
recommendation: Move the net-of-recovery examples to the recovery variant or re-base them, as R218 recommended; this build still shows it.

issue: The same misfire. The guessed split gives natural gas 0.332 GJ/t against the hosts 0.022, and coke-oven gas 3.32 against 4.01, so the fuel-emission-factor identity returns 0.895 t/t against the hosts 0.2023 - an efficient variant 4.4 times dirtier than its host.
benchmark: Coke-oven underfiring CO2 is 0.15 to 0.3 t/t coke, and the efficient variant should sit at or below the host
recommendation: Same fix as IS009: scale the hosts carrier split, do not replace it.

value-in-db: share-to-capture 62.5 % (range 50-75, n=1, estimated); emissions-captured 0.8666 t/t; SEC steam 2.036 GJ/t
issue: A no-capture archetype carries a full capture set. The 62.5% is the midpoint of etsap_2010_007s printed CO2 abatement range of 50-75% (tp-etsap_2010_007-0004), which is an abatement percentage, not the share of the furnaces CO2 sent to a capture plant; the example id itself reads blast-furnace_top-gas-recycling-ccs. emissions-captured 0.8666 comes from the IEAGHG MDEA-PZ case and the 2.036 GJ/t steam is that cases amine reboiler.
benchmark: Share sent to capture is defined in decisions.md 2026-10-05 as captured divided by capture rate times host CO2; an abatement range cannot be read into it
recommendation: Either move the capture rows to a TGR-with-capture variant, or re-read the ETSAP row as emissions-reduction-potential. Extends R235 of the 2026-10-04 pass, which flagged the steam row only.

issue: The pool mixes three bases. agora_2021_001 0.5 is per t crude steel including the EAF step (tp-agora_2021_001-0007) and material-economics_2019_001 1.1 is per t steel including casting and hot rolling (tp-material-economics_2019_001-0005), while rechberger_2020_001 gives 0.453 per t DRI for the gas-reformer case and 0.040 for the electric-heater case. Ruling S80 of 2026-10-05 set aside the Agora per-steel values on reactor_steel-offgas-chemicals but not this one.
benchmark: Natural-gas DRI direct CO2 is 0.45 to 0.60 t/t DRI (Rechberger 0.453; Midrex about 0.55)
recommendation: Set aside the two per-t-crude-steel examples, and move the 0.040 electric-heater case to the hydrogen or electric DRI archetype. The central survives by luck, but the band is meaningless and the derived share-to-capture of 58.3% on the CCS child uses this total as its denominator.

issue: An efficient variant 31 points less efficient than its host. The value is the top-ranked pick from pfeifer_2002_001s 1990 energy balance of a 60 t furnace, a thermal efficiency on total input including chemical energy, while the hosts electric-arc-furnace efficiency of 83.98% (n=22) is an electrical figure. The two are not the same ratio.
benchmark: Scrap preheating raises EAF efficiency; on a consistent basis the variant should be at or above the hosts 84 %
recommendation: Tag the efficiency basis on both rows, or drop the Pfeifer thermal balance from this cell and let the bucket-saving rule derive the variant from the host.

value-in-db: 0.022192 GJ/t (n=1) in wide-archetype.csv; a second row holds 0.199728-1.19837 with no central
issue: The same duplicate-key defect as IS004. One row is the sum of the carriers of remus_2013_001 (0.022192); the other is range only from two aries_2024_001 foundry ladle-preheating examples (0.1997 to 1.1984). wide-archetype.csv keeps the first and drops the range, so the archetype carries no band at all.
benchmark: Ladle preheating is 0.02 to 0.1 GJ/t liquid steel in an integrated mill; the foundry figures are on a different denominator
recommendation: Fix the duplicate key as in IS004, and decide whether the foundry examples belong on this archetype. R273 of 2026-10-04 asked for the 1.08 example to be excluded; it is now in a second, parallel row instead.

issue: The hot blast from the stoves is carried as a heat carrier, marked pooled apart: not part of the split of the total, so it does not sum with the others. That is deliberate, but the stove fuel is blast-furnace gas that is already inside the coke and coal rows, so a modeller who sums the carrier columns of wide-archetype-carriers-species.csv double-counts 4.52 on a 13.63 GJ/t furnace, a 33% overstatement. blast-furnace_ccs-diffuse inherits it at 4.69882.
benchmark: Hot blast is an internal stream, not a purchased carrier; the furnaces purchased energy is the 13.63 GJ/t of coke, coal, and electricity
recommendation: Mark internal streams explicitly in the carrier output (a flag column or a separate internal-stream table) so they cannot be summed with purchased carriers.

issue: Still present from R290 of 2026-10-04 and now higher (was 6.4). A route built on electrolytic hydrogen carries 7.1 GJ/t of natural gas, which is most of a full gas-DRI gas demand; the carriers also sum to 21.95 GJ/t against a total of 12.96.
benchmark: Hydrogen DRI with EAF uses 0 to 1 GJ/t of natural gas (Vogl 2018 nil)
recommendation: As R290: check the Otto 2017 case definitions and exclude the row if it is the gas-DRI or hybrid case.

issue: The level-2 fuel split gives natural gas 100% of fuel, but the splitting example (gielen_1997_001 Table 2.3.10) prints fuel 1.55 GJ/t and natural gas only 0.2 GJ/t (0.222 after the HHV uplift). The split renormalises a partial named-fuel set to the whole of fuel, so 1.33 GJ/t of unspecified fuel is relabelled as natural gas.
benchmark: Natural gas 0.222 GJ/t as the example states it, with the rest left in fuel or in not-stated
recommendation: In carriers.py, scale the named fuels only where they account for most of fuel; otherwise keep the stated values and put the remainder in not-stated. The same mechanism affects furnace_hybrid-electric, furnace_oxy-fuel, furnace_tempering, furnace_lehr, and distillery_beverage-spirits, where fuel is handed wholly to natural gas.

issue: The carrier split for this variant is incoherent: the three named fuels sum to 2.06 GJ/t against a fuel figure of 5.99, and the largest of them is a judgement guess on a variant whose host names no petroleum coke.
benchmark: The named fuels should sum to fuel 5.99, split as the host kiln_lime-rotary-preheater is split
recommendation: Derive the variant's fuel split from the host rather than guessing a carrier, and drop the petroleum-coke guess.

issue: The central is derived from captured-and-emitted pairs, which is the documented intent, but the low and high are still the pooled values of the thirteen examples that state a CAPTURE RATE (40, 50, 65, 80, 85, 90 x5, 95 x3, 100). Central and band therefore measure two different quantities, and the band reads as though the share could be 51%.
benchmark: Either a band derived the same way as the central, or no band at all
recommendation: Derive the band from the same captured-and-emitted pairs, or blank it and say in central-from that the stated rates are a different quantity. The cement central is no longer the 97% from four examples recorded as the open item; it is 99.75% from six derived pairs in this build.

issue: The pooled total sits below the archetype's own combustion 0.2067 plus process 0.18 (0.387), because the median of four includes tp-van-geene_2024_001-0015, card TC0003, a GREEN-GAS regenerative furnace whose 0.0394 t/t is process emissions only. A biomethane furnace does not belong in the pool for the conventional air-fuel furnace.
benchmark: A gas-fired regenerative furnace at 5.2 GJ/t emits about 0.26 t CO2/t from combustion plus 0.12-0.2 process, so 0.38-0.46 t/t; wsp_2015_003 gives 0.334 for melting alone
recommendation: Exclude TC0003 from furnace_regenerative, or give renewable-gas firing its own variant. Then check the total against combustion plus process.

issue: The single sourced total (wsp_2015_003 p.34 Table 6) is five times below the archetype's own combustion figure of 0.0942 t/t, which the fuel-emission-factor identity derives from 1.861 GJ/t of natural gas. One of the two is on the wrong basis; the WSP lehr figure is most likely per tonne of total site product rather than per tonne through the lehr.
benchmark: An annealing lehr burning 1.86 GJ/t of gas emits about 0.09-0.10 t CO2/t
recommendation: Re-read the WSP table to confirm the denominator; if it is site product, exclude it and let the identity stand.

value-in-db: two rows: one blank central with low 0.599184 and high 1.59782, one central 0.793213 with no band
issue: The archetype, parameter, target and unit key is not unique: the giner-santonja_2019_001 BREF range (0.15-0.40 MWh per t beet) and the rehfeldt_2018_001 carrier sum sit in two separate rows. wide-archetype keeps 0.793213 and drops the band, so the modeller sees a central with no uncertainty while a perfectly good range is in the file. Six such duplicate keys exist across the build.
benchmark: One row per archetype, parameter, target and unit, with the BREF range as the band around 0.79
recommendation: Merge the range-only row into the central row in summarise or assembly, and add a build check that the key is unique. The cf-beet-per-sugar factor of 7.19 itself traces correctly: 4.50 GJ per t sugar becomes 0.694 GJ per t beet after the HHV uplift.

value-in-db: 50, 32.5 and 32.5 years against the host kiln's 25
issue: Three variants of the dry precalciner kiln outlive their host, the capture retrofit by a factor of two. A retrofit cannot have a longer economic life than the plant it sits on, and the 50 years from rootzen_2017_001 is almost certainly the cement plant's life rather than the capture unit's.
benchmark: A capture retrofit takes the shorter of its own life and the host's remaining life, so at most 25 years here
recommendation: Cap a variant's lifetime at its host's, or name the host's 25 years explicitly for these three. This also lowers the ccs levelized cost, which currently amortises over 50 years.

issue: The moderate efficiency bucket is more efficient than the strong one. Both are single-source range midpoints (ECRA 2009 and MPA 2011) on what are probably different definitions of thermal efficiency, so they cannot be compared as they stand, yet they sit side by side as siblings.
benchmark: A strong efficiency variant must be at least as efficient as the moderate one, and both above the base 59.9%
recommendation: Check what each source means by efficiency and put the two buckets on one definition, or drop efficiency for these variants and rely on specific-energy-consumption, where the ordering (3.43 moderate, 2.90 strong) is right.

issue: Both come from stuckrath_2022_001, but 0.182 GJ of electricity per GJ of cooling is a COP of 5.5, not 4.1. The identity used for chiller_high-efficiency (total = 100 / efficiency) is not applied here, so the archetype states two incompatible performance figures.
benchmark: 0.244 GJ/GJ at a COP of 4.1, or an efficiency of 549% at 0.182 GJ/GJ
recommendation: Apply the same identity to this archetype, or trace which of the two figures Stuckrath and Worrell actually print for the conventional plant.

value-in-db: pulp lime kiln 0.58235 t/t and 8.40688 GJ/t; mineral lime kilns 0.785 t/t and 4.05-6.31 GJ/t
issue: Checking the lime overlap the brief asks about: every lime kiln in non-metallic-minerals carries the stoichiometric 0.785 t CO2 per t CaO from the CLM BREF, while the pulp-and-paper lime kiln carries 0.58235 (band 0.552-0.690). The chemistry is the same, so the pulp figure looks to be per tonne of lime mud or on a partly calcined basis. The pulp kiln's 8.41 GJ/t is also above every mineral lime kiln and above the usual range.
benchmark: Calcining CaCO3 releases 0.785 t CO2 per t of pure CaO, less the non-carbonate content, so 0.70-0.785; pulp-mill lime kilns use 5.5-7.5 GJ/t CaO
recommendation: Pass this to the pulp-and-paper reviewer: check the denominator on the kiln_lime-rotary process-emission and energy examples, and align the two families on one lime basis.

value-in-db: 967.61 and 1060.63 CAD/t for the electric furnace, 753-829 for the regenerative, 77-133 for the oxy-fuel
issue: Glass melting's levelized costs are the highest in the three families and sit above the selling price of the glass. Three inputs compound: the Gielen whole-product variable opex of MC001, a capex of 1110 CAD per annual tonne for the electric furnace (high 6644), and a sourced lifetime of 7 years pooled from electrode campaign lives. The oxy-fuel furnace, which escapes the Gielen row, comes out an order of magnitude lower, which shows the size of the effect.
benchmark: Container and flat glass production cost 250-450 CAD/t, of which melting is roughly half
recommendation: Fix MC001 first, then re-read the capex band and decide whether a furnace campaign life (2-7 years) or an asset life (12-20 years with rebuilds) belongs in the levelized-cost denominator. Worth asking Brad which he wants the model to see.

issue: The single example, tp-cusano_2017_001-... from p.820 Table 8.5, is a ferro-alloy furnace and the note says "gross consumption per t of tapped alloy, furnace process only". The archetype's product is titanium slag, a different product with a different energy requirement, and the submerged-arc sibling guess (18.8 GJ/t) was drafted off it.
benchmark: Ilmenite smelting to titanium slag about 2.4-2.9 MWh/t slag (8.6-10.4 GJ/t)
recommendation: Confirm with Brad whether this archetype is ilmenite smelting or a ferro-alloy furnace; if titanium slag, re-source it and re-draft the submerged-arc sibling.

issue: The hydrogen carrier comes from mpp_2023_001 Exhibit TA3.2 with source-technology calciner_hydrogen-fired, an archetype that no longer exists (prior finding R371 reviewed it); the merge left a hydrogen-fired alternative's fuel demand on a gas-fired calciner, where it exceeds the archetype's own total and is priced into cost-levelized calculated-incl-energy (139.5 CAD/t, hydrogen 3.854 GJ x 24.22). The ccs variant inherits it.
benchmark: A gas-suspension calciner uses 2.9-3.3 GJ/t alumina of gas and no hydrogen
recommendation: Move the hydrogen rows to a hydrogen-fired calciner archetype or set them aside as an alternative fuel case, and keep them out of the levelized energy cost.

issue: All four come from bcs_2007_001 Exhibits 23-25, where the note records the definition: theoretical minimum energy divided by actual. That is a second-law ratio, not the conversion efficiency the parameter means elsewhere, and 1 % on a mill reads as a broken machine. The same exhibits' SEC rows were ruled out for the per-ton-of-material-handled basis (R651) on flotation only: ventilation still pools 3.49e-06 GJ/t (R650) and grinding still pools 18.7 kWh/t.
benchmark: A comminution circuit has no model-usable conversion efficiency; grinding is 1-3 % efficient only in the second-law sense
recommendation: Either tag these as a separate parameter (comminution or second-law efficiency) or drop them, and apply the R651 material-handled exclusion to the ventilation, hoisting and grinding rows from the same exhibits. Prior finding R655 recorded the 1 %.

issue: The heat carrier alone exceeds the total and the description's 17-20 GJ/t (screen-carriers ratio 2.3). The electricity central 22.192 is in fact the cusano_2017_001 p.909 whole-process figure of 20 GJ/t (all carriers, HHV-adjusted), and the only true electricity example, 5 MWh/t from p.952, is printed per t of nickel, copper AND cobalt produced, not per t nickel.
benchmark: Nickel matte refining 17-20 GJ/t Ni in total, of which 3-4 MWh/t electricity
recommendation: Untag the 20 GJ/t row from electricity, re-read the p.952 heat and electricity ranges, and note the Ni+Cu+Co basis. Prior finding R394 recorded the heat overshoot.

archetype: (22 of 66 archetypes, e.g. smelting-vessel_flash, digester_bayer, electrolysis-cell_zinc-electrowinning)
value-in-db: e.g. flash carriers = natural-gas while the SEC rows give electricity 3.52 and natural-gas 1.68
issue: The archetype table's carriers field disagrees with the carriers that actually carry a pooled SEC on a third of the family. Electricity is missing from flash, bath-tuyere, bottom-blowing, top-submerged-lance and open-arc smelting; coal, diesel, oil and heavy fuel oil are missing from digester_bayer; coke, natural gas and oil are missing from zinc electrowinning; and solar, coke, steam and biomass are listed where no row exists.
benchmark: The two lists should agree, or the metadata field should be derived from the SEC rows
recommendation: Derive the carriers field from the pooled SEC targets at build time instead of maintaining it by hand. S94 covers the solar and coke entries only.

value-in-db: rows excluded with "no conversion from kWh/t ore", "from GJ/t-hydrate", "from kg/t ore", "from L/t"
issue: Good sourced rows are dropped for want of four factors: kWh/t ore and kg/t ore (norgate_2010_001 grinding 18.5 kWh/t, flotation 7.5 kWh/t, hauling 2.0-2.2 kg/t), GJ/t-hydrate (riotinto_2022_001 1.66 GJ/t-hydrate for both the gas and hydrogen calciner cases), and the diesel volume units of NM011. The per-t-ore rows matter most because they are the only external check on the NRCan and BCS mining values.
benchmark: kWh/t ore is dimensionally GJ/t ore once the archetype basis is ore; 1.53 t hydrate per t alumina; diesel 38.7 MJ/L
recommendation: Add an ore-basis alias so kWh/t ore maps to GJ/t on ore-product archetypes, add cf-hydrate-per-alumina, and add the diesel volume factors.

issue: A pure judgement draft with a 10x band, and its product unit is t concentrate while both leaching siblings are per t metal, so the three cannot be compared. The capex is 4,500x the family median and drives a levelized cost of 18,446 CAD/t.
benchmark: In-situ recovery for uranium or copper is roughly 5-30 GJ per t of metal, well below the heap and HPAL routes on a per-t-metal basis
recommendation: Ask Brad for the intended product basis, then re-draft the SEC and capex against the heap-leach archetype rather than freehand.

issue: The sub-carriers sum to 54 % more than the fuel carrier they belong to, because each was bucket-scaled from a different remus_2013_001 example. The archetype also sits in mining while all its proxies are iron-and-steel pellet plants, so a modeller comparing mining archetypes meets an induration furnace.
benchmark: The sub-carriers of a fuel total should sum to it; induration fuel is 0.5-0.9 GJ/t pellets
recommendation: Scale the sub-carriers to the fuel total after bucketing, and confirm the pellet plant belongs in the mining family.

issue: The central is van-geene_2024_001 with no low or high, and it is 22 % above the prebaked cell (53.7 GJ/t, 14.9 MWh/t). An inert anode raises the cell's theoretical demand by about 20 %, but the developers' case and the MPP pathway both assume a wettable cathode and better current efficiency alongside it, landing at or below the incumbent.
benchmark: 12.5-14 MWh/t Al (45-50 GJ/t) in MPP and the Elysis case; up to 16 MWh/t only without the cathode change
recommendation: Re-read the three pooled examples, separate anode-only from anode-plus-cathode cases, and give the archetype a band. Prior finding R377 called the 65.6 primary energy.

issue: Both centrals are the SF6 cover gas alone, converted at a 1990s GWP: 0.0006 t SF6/t x 23,900 = 14.34 and 0.00089 x 23,900 = 21.27, from nccp_1999_002. They are presented as the process emission of the archetype, so a modeller reads a magnesium cell as emitting 14 t CO2e/t with no CO2 line at all.
benchmark: SF6 was replaced by SO2 or HFC-134a after 2000; modern cover-gas emissions are 0.1-1 t CO2e/t Mg, and the route's CO2 comes from the reductant and the power
recommendation: Tag these as cover-gas SF6 (species sf6 only, which is already stored), add the route's CO2, and say in the note that they describe 1990s practice. Prior finding R395 recorded the Pidgeon case.

issue: The icf_2015_001 Table 3-8 rows enter the pool twice for each device, once "with credit for recovered gas" and once "without credit", and the pooling treats them as two independent observations. For pump_plunger-lift the central of 260 CAD/t-CH4 is simply the midpoint of -4.88 (with credit) and 525.78 (without credit), which is neither definition and matches no published figure.
benchmark: An abatement cost is defined either net of the recovered gas or gross; the two differ by the gas price times the recovery and should not be averaged.
recommendation: Pick one convention for abatement-cost (net of recovered gas reads most naturally against CIMS fuel prices), keep the other as a set-aside, and record the ruling in docs/decisions.md.

issue: The central is "top-ranked: Aranda et al. 2014" and equals the maximum of its own band, while the three etsap_2010_012 rows in the same pool give 21.4-46.2 CAD/GJ-per-yr. The band 21.4-142.7 is therefore not an uncertainty range but two incompatible readings of CTL capital cost sitting side by side.
benchmark: The Aranda figure (1220 USD2013/kW of coal input, bridged through 49% efficiency) works out to about USD 167,000 per bbl/d, which matches built CTL plants; the ETSAP rows are 4-7x lower (see OG006).
recommendation: Resolve the ETSAP basis first (OG006). If it is wrong, exclude the ETSAP capex rows here too so the band reflects real spread.

issue: The drafted total is 2.9x the base-load sibling's 4.1 GJ/t and 22% of the HHV of the LNG produced. The natural-gas carrier (10.95 GJ/t, range midpoint of five zhang_2020_001 rows) is the "primary energy input" of the worst single-expander designs at 28.8% turbine efficiency, which is not a small-scale plant's usual duty.
benchmark: LNG plant self-consumption is 8-12% of feed, so about 4.5-7 GJ/t LNG; small-scale plants sit at the top of that, not at 12 GJ/t.
recommendation: Rebase the small-scale total on the gas-turbine-driven rows nearest a real small-scale plant, or hold it at about 7 GJ/t and widen the band; ask Brad whether the single-expander designs belong to this archetype at all.

issue: Two emissions-combustion rows for one archetype differ by 9x. The co2 row is the identity from the archetype's 5.65 GJ/m3 of natural gas; the co2e row is the midpoint of ceri_2017_002's "potential GHG intensity of 0-10 kgCO2e/bbl", which is the post-capture intensity of the SEGD concept, not a combustion emission. Nothing in the record says which is net, and the archetype carries no emissions-captured or share-to-capture row to reconcile them. Its efficiency and emissions-reduction-potential rows also draw their single example from boiler_direct-contact, a different archetype, and both come out blank.
benchmark: Down-hole oxy-combustion burns gas in the reservoir and leaves the CO2 there, so the right shape is a gross combustion CO2 of about 0.29 t/m3 plus emissions-captured and share-to-capture, netting to the 0-10 kgCO2e/bbl the source reports.
recommendation: Re-map the 0-10 kgCO2e/bbl row to emissions-captured or to a net-emissions parameter, and re-check why boiler_direct-contact examples are feeding this archetype's efficiency and reduction potential.

issue: Four family rows carry n of 1 and grade sourced but no central, low, or high: drilling-rig_electric emissions-reduction-potential (ipieca_2025_001), flare abatement-cost co2e (anl_2017_001), and well_in-situ-oxy-combustion efficiency and emissions-reduction-potential (ceri_2017_002). The build has 53 such rows in all, so this is a pipeline behaviour, not a family one: an example that carries a unit or a note but no number still creates a pooled row.
benchmark: A pooled row with no central should either not be written or should be written with grade unfilled so coverage.csv does not count it as sourced.
recommendation: Fix the pooling step to skip example rows with no value, or to emit them to the unfilled/ folder; worth raising once for the whole build rather than per family.

archetype: turboexpander_ngl-recovery; pump_plunger-lift; pump_artificial-lift; pump_electric-station; adsorber_molecular-sieve; drilling-rig_diesel
issue: Three fill analogues look wrong for this family. turboexpander_ngl-recovery takes 38.05% from turboexpander_pressure-let-down, a let-down machine that runs on spare pressure, while an NGL recovery turboexpander runs at its gas plant's availability. The two pumps, the plunger lift, and the molecular-sieve dehydrator all take 60.025% from a four-member "rotating-equipment" class median whose members are a CO2 dehydration compressor, a waste-heat recovery unit, an induction motor, and a let-down turboexpander. The three drilling rigs take 90% from the all-archetype median of 96.
benchmark: Gas plant dehydration, NGL recovery, and pipeline pump stations run at 90-95%. Canadian drilling rig utilisation averages 40-60% (CAODC), so 90% overstates annual metres drilled and understates cost per metre by about 1.6x.
recommendation: Give turboexpander_ngl-recovery, adsorber_molecular-sieve, and pump_electric-station the gas-treatment-unit sibling capacity factor of 95%, and set the drilling rigs from a rig utilisation figure rather than the all-archetype median.

issue: For the methane and flaring archetypes the wide view carries two costs on the same quantity, a cost-levelized calculated from capex and opex per t of CH4 or CO2 and a sourced abatement-cost on the same tonne, and they disagree in both directions: 25x low for separator_reduced-emission-completion, 53x high for compressor_flare-gas-recovery, 6.5x high for compressor_low-emission-seal, against 1.2x for management-system_leak-detection and 0.6x for flare_enclosed-combustor, which are consistent. A modeller cannot tell which of the two to use.
benchmark: The two should agree within the gas credit (the abatement cost is the levelized cost less the value of the recovered gas) once both are on the same tonne.
recommendation: Add a check to the build comparing cost-levelized calculated with abatement-cost for every archetype whose product is t CH4 or t CO2, and report the ratio next to coverage; the outliers it finds are usually a denominator problem like OG003.

issue: The drafted output of 700 t CO2/yr corresponds to about 37,000 m3/yr of gas burned, roughly 100 m3/day, which is a pilot rather than a working flare. Because the capex guesses of 300 and 500 CAD per t/yr were drafted against that output, both the implied total capital (about CAD 210,000 and 350,000, which is reasonable for a stack) and the per-tonne cost move together, so the per-tonne figure the modeller sees is about 10-30x too high.
benchmark: Reported Canadian flare volumes run 1,000-10,000 m3/day per flare (AER ST60B, ECCC inventory), which is 7,000-70,000 t CO2/yr; on a plausible stack cost that puts capex nearer 5-50 CAD per t/yr.
recommendation: Redraft the flare and flare_high-efficiency annual outputs from reported per-flare volumes and rescale the capex guesses to keep the implied total capital, or ask Brad which flare size the archetype should represent.

issue: Still a single sourced row with no band, built on a capacity of 4.33 t CH4/yr for a whole liner programme. R554 of the 2026-10-04 pass benchmarked the same value at 50,000-150,000 USD per t/yr and marked it low; the gap is 10-30x, which is a wrong-denominator gap rather than a cosmetic one.
benchmark: Natural Gas STAR cites USD 30-60 per foot for liners, about USD 200,000-300,000 per mile, avoiding 1-4 t CH4/yr.
recommendation: Re-extract the liner length and the avoided methane from the same STAR passage so the denominator matches the cost, and raise the severity of R554.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
value-in-db: 3.6 GJ/t (n=18 on the carrier, n=1 on the total)
issue: The central comes from one Cusano et al. 2017 channel-induction row (cusano_2017_001, pp.418-419, Table 4.28) at 3.6 GJ/t, taken as "sum of the carriers" and then copied onto the electricity carrier as a 100% share, which discards the other 17 electricity examples. Those cluster at 1.29-3.02 GJ/t (Kermeli et al. 2016 p.67 at 1.865, p.55 at 3.024, NCCP 1999 at 1.728, Kermeli p.78 at 1.598-1.745, Cusano channel-induction charge at 1.29), so the pooled value is about twice the population median. The archetype also mixes ferrous melting (762 kWh/short-ton of steel) with aluminium (Btu/lb) on one t-of-metal product unit.
benchmark: Induction melting 500-600 kWh/t of iron or steel (1.8-2.2 GJ/t); aluminium 0.6-1.0 GJ/t (Cusano et al. 2017 NFM BREF, Kermeli et al. 2016)
recommendation: Let the total take the median of the example set (about 1.8 GJ/t) rather than the carrier-split row, and check whether the archetype should be split by metal.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
value-in-db: alkylation steam 1.59724 with fuel 1.60425 against a total of 1.63713; isomerization steam 1.13099 with fuel 1.23199 against a total of 1.27745
issue: On both archetypes the steam row is pooled apart from the split, so fuel plus steam plus electricity comes to about twice the total (screen-carriers ratios 1.976 and 1.885). Refinery steam use is reported either as a separate utility or already inside the fuel-equivalent total depending on the source (Energetics 1998 sets the share, while the steam medians come from Gary 2007, Meyers 1997, PRELIM, and REF BREF), and the build mixes the two conventions. Recorded as R515 on the then-combined reactor_alkylation-isomerization archetype; the split into two archetypes has not fixed it.
benchmark: Alkylation about 1.6-2.3 GJ/m3 and isomerization about 0.5-1.0 GJ/m3 in total, with steam counted once
recommendation: Decide whether steam sits inside the fuel-equivalent total or beside it, and either include the steam row in the split or mark the total as fuel-equivalent so a consumer does not add them.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The band spans 284 times, which makes it useless for anything but the central. A high of 3,396 CAD per GJ/yr of hydrogen is roughly forty times a plausible installed cost and a low of 12 is about eight times too cheap, so the pool is almost certainly mixing stack-only with full-system costs and rated-electrical with delivered-hydrogen denominators. The same archetype also carries an abatement cost of 1,991.71 CAD/t-CO2-eq from a two-row pool whose low is 139.9, with the central pinned at the top of the range.
benchmark: PEM or alkaline system 1,200-2,200 USD/kW_e, which at 70% HHV efficiency is about 90-180 CAD per GJ/yr of hydrogen at a 50-100% capacity factor; green-hydrogen abatement 150-600 CAD/t
recommendation: Tag each capex example with its basis (stack against system, rated kW_e against delivered GJ H2) as S87 proposes for the renewables, then re-pool; take the abatement cost as the median of the two rows rather than the top.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
value-in-db: 13 examples excluded for want of a conversion
issue: Thirteen IEAGHG 2017 rows (ieaghg_2017_002, PDF p.42, Table 4-7) are dropped with "no conversion from Gcal/t-feed to GJ/m3" and "no conversion from kWh/t-feed to GJ/m3". They are the only reference-refinery rows in the pool and would have anchored the central, which currently rests on MIDDEN cards and two IEA rows. The missing step is a feed density, which the build already holds for crude (cf-crude-volume is used on the MIDDEN rows in the same archetype).
benchmark: Gas oil and vacuum residue feed density 0.86-0.98 t/m3; the IEAGHG rows at 0.033-0.214 Gcal/t-feed come to about 0.12-0.9 GJ/m3, squarely in the expected range
recommendation: Add a feed-density conversion factor for refinery unit feeds (or allow cf-crude-volume on t-feed units) so the IEAGHG reference-refinery rows pool.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
value-in-db: capex 4.8116 CAD/GJ-per-yr; capacity 0.16 MW; lifetime 25 years; efficiency 91.0238%
issue: Every sourced value on this industrial space-heating archetype comes from DEA 2026 residential and apartment heating sheets (dea_2026_007, sheets "201 Oil boiler, ex apart" and "202 Gas boiler, ex apart" and "new apart"), which are 160-320 kW apartment-complex boilers, not the unit heaters and make-up air units the archetype rationale describes. The LHV to HHV conversion is handled properly (101% LHV becomes 91.02% HHV), so the efficiency is sound, but the capacity, capex, and lifetime describe a different machine. The archetype also has named fuel carriers (natural-gas, oil) with no aggregate fuel row, unlike its siblings, which is why screen-carriers reads a ratio of 0.1 for it.
benchmark: Industrial gas unit heaters 80-85% HHV and condensing make-up air 90-95%, 30-300 kW, 15-20 year life, roughly 3-8 CAD per GJ/yr
recommendation: Keep the DEA efficiency, flag the capacity and lifetime as borrowed from a residential boiler, and add an ASHRAE or equipment-vendor unit-heater cost; add the aggregate fuel row so the carrier screen reads it correctly.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The class-median and sibling lifetime fills carry lows of 1 to 1.5 years because measure lives and programme horizons sit in the same pools as equipment service lives (UKERC 2013, McKane and Hasanbeigi 2010, and Martin et al. 2000 measure lives on the motor variant). The 2026-10-04 pass reached the same conclusion on steam-cracker_fired-tubular and electrolysis-cell_iron-electrowinning (S10 and S11: "sibling estimate contaminated by stack/measure-horizon lives"), and the contamination is still in the pools that feed these fills.
benchmark: Air handlers and cooling towers 20-25 years, electric compressor drives 20-25 years, motors 15-25 years; no such equipment has a one-year life
recommendation: Give measure lives and programme horizons a species of their own, as the hours-based lifetimes now get (that fix works: lighting_fluorescent-hid, haul-truck_hydrogen-fuel-cell, and fuel-cell_chp all carry component or stack species), and exclude them from the equipment-lifetime pools the fill rules read.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The two sourced whole-refinery archetypes carry totals that are the Gary et al. 2007 electricity figure alone, with the refinery-gas and natural-gas rows drafted at zero (highs of 0.9-2.0), so a hydroskimming refinery reads 0.041 GJ/m3 against the drafted refinery_conversion at 2.8. The spread across the three archetypes is 68 times for what should be a graded set. This is S98, still open and still showing in this build.
benchmark: Hydroskimming about 1.5-2.5 GJ/m3 of crude, conversion 2.5-3.5, deep conversion 3.5-5 (about 4-10% of crude energy content)
recommendation: Re-extract the Gary et al. 2007 refinery tables for the fuel rows, or mark the two sourced totals as electricity-only and let the drafted fuel rows carry a real central so the three archetypes order correctly.

issue: GJ/ODt and kWh/ODt convert only where a product-ratio factor rides along. The same NRCan 2008 mill survey converts on evaporator_multiple-effect and boiler_recovery, where cf-bls-per-pulp carries the oven-dry to air-dry step inside it, but is dropped on debarker_drum and kiln_lime-rotary with 'no conversion from GJ/ODt to GJ/t' (tp-nrcan_2008_001-0001 to -0004 and -0021 to -0026). The oven-dry step is bundled into the solids ratio instead of standing on its own, so Canada's own mill benchmark survey is excluded from the lime kiln and the woodyard.
benchmark: 1 ODt = 1.111 ADt, which is already implied by the 1.6667 divisor the pipeline uses on the NRCan evaporator rows.
recommendation: Add ODt to ADt as a standalone conversion in records/reference/conversion-factor.csv and let it compose with cf-lime-per-pulp and the wood basis, so the NRCan rows reach kiln_lime-rotary and debarker_drum.

value-in-db: total 26.8 GJ/t air-dry pulp against an electricity carrier of 5.76
issue: The total is Martin et al. 2000 (pulp and paper) and the split is Suhr et al. 2015 PP BREF (suhr_2015_001:pulper_chemi-thermomechanical@non-integrated-ctmp-mill-finland-400-ml-csf), 4.3 times apart. CTMP refining is an electricity-dominated step and the thermomechanical sibling pulper_thermomechanical sits at 8.05 GJ/t with electricity 7.17, so a CTMP figure of 26.8 GJ/t is out of line with its nearest relative by more than three times. Martin's number reads like a whole-mill or primary-energy total.
benchmark: CTMP refining draws about 1,800-2,800 kWh/ADt, i.e. 6.5-10 GJ/t of electricity, plus up to about 1 GJ/t of steam; the BREF value of 5.76 GJ/t is at the low end of that and is the credible one.
recommendation: Re-read the Martin et al. 2000 row for scope and, if it is whole-mill or primary energy, exclude it and let the BREF split set the total. Check the sibling pulper_thermomechanical's Martin rows at the same time.

issue: The low comes from Fleiter et al. 2012 (tp-fleiter_2012_001-0045), whose note reads 'Electrical efficiency about 10-15 % (electricity per black liquor energy input)'. The row's target is blank, so an electrical efficiency range pools into the all-carrier thermal efficiency and its 10 % minimum becomes 8.97 % after the LHV to HHV step. The same quantity from Larson et al. 2006 is correctly targeted to electricity and sits in the separate efficiency_electricity value of 12.02 %.
benchmark: A Tomlinson recovery boiler converts 64-75 % of the liquor's heating value into steam; the pooled band should run about 55-79 %.
recommendation: Set target to electricity on tp-fleiter_2012_001-0045 so it joins efficiency_electricity, and add a check that flags an efficiency band whose low is below a quarter of its central.

issue: Vakkilainen's steam-generation efficiencies are excluded with 'reported on a lower-heating-value basis; records/reference/heating-value-stream.csv names no fuel or product for this archetype' (tp-vakkilainen_2006_001-0013, -0017, -0021), yet the same source's same-table rows on the sibling boiler_recovery (87.3, 87.6, 87.9 %) convert without complaint to 78.3-78.8 %. Same source, same parameter, same basis, two outcomes, so the high-solids variant ends up pooling only three loosely sourced values.
benchmark: The three excluded rows should land near 79 % on an HHV basis, as their boiler_recovery twins do.
recommendation: Give boiler_recovery-high-solids the same black-liquor entry in heating-value-stream.csv that boiler_recovery has, then re-run. Check whether any other variant pair is split the same way.

issue: The two values are the same physical quantity, the heating value of a tonne of black liquor solids, and they differ by 14 % only because of how the two sources were handled. IEAGHG's 25.48 GJ/ADt took cf-hhv-lhv-black-liquor and the 1.86 ratio to reach 15.27 (tp-ieaghg_2016_001-0047); Francis et al. 2002's 21.0 GJ/ADt took the 1.6 ratio and no heating-value step, since its note says the basis is not applicable, to reach 13.125 (tp-francis_2002_001-0029). A modeller reading the two archetypes sees the high-solids boiler saving 2.1 GJ of liquor per tonne of solids, which is not a saving a high-solids boiler can make: high-solids firing raises steam output and efficiency, not the liquor's heating value.
benchmark: Kraft black liquor solids hold about 13.5-14.5 GJ/t on an HHV basis, so both archetypes should carry the same figure and the variant's gain should show up in efficiency and steam output instead.
recommendation: Check whether Francis's 6,250 Btu/lb of solids is HHV or LHV and apply cf-hhv-lhv-black-liquor if it is LHV, then pool the liquor heating value once across the recovery-boiler archetypes rather than per variant. Fixing PB017 will also give the variant a proper efficiency to carry the difference.

value-in-db: 0.509 GJ/t from a single example; 6 rows dropped
issue: Every mechanical vapour recompression example is stated per tonne of water evaporated and all of them drop out: JRC 2009 (tp-jrc_2009_001-0054 to -0057) and Alcoa (tp-alcoa_2024_001-0005, tp-alcoa_2022_001-0010, -0015, -0019, 46-57 kWh per t water), leaving only Van Geene et al. 2024's 0.509 GJ/t BLS. The archetype's whole evidence base rests on one row because of a missing conversion, and both spellings of the unit, with a space and with a hyphen, fail separately.
benchmark: Evaporating about 2.5 t of water per t of black liquor solids at 50 kWh per t of water gives roughly 0.45 GJ/t BLS, which brackets the surviving value and would let the excluded rows confirm it.
recommendation: Add a water-evaporated per t BLS conversion factor, and make kWh/t water evaporated and kWh/t-water-evaporated one unit. Alcoa's rows are alumina, not pulp, so check the host before pooling them.

issue: One DOE 2023 range is the sole source for four unrelated measures, two of them on paper machines, one on refining and one on evaporation. A single generic number stamped on four technologies with very different capital and savings is not an abatement cost for any of them, and all four are negative, so each will look free in any ranking built from this column.
benchmark: Measure-specific abatement costs in pulp and paper span roughly -150 to +200 CAD/t CO2; a shoe press and an MVR evaporator should not share a value.
recommendation: Either compute abatement cost per archetype from its own capex, savings and emission factor, or drop the DOE 2023 rows and leave the field empty rather than carry one number four times.

issue: Both come only from Svensson et al. 2021, which prices, for the same 121.5 kt CaO/yr mill, 55.8 M EUR for the rotary kiln (tp-svensson_2021_001-0014) and 23.3 M EUR for the plasma kiln (tp-svensson_2021_001-0002). The source is internally consistent, but the result is that the conventional, mature Canadian lime kiln is 2.4 times the capital of a prospective electrified one, which will push any CIMS market share towards the electric kiln on capital alone. The two Canadian cost rows that could check it, Owttrim et al. 2022 and Kuparinen et al. 2017, are both set aside as incremental and needing a host. The cost-ratio backtest also fails hard here: it expects 53.7 CAD/t-per-yr of fixed opex against the sourced 3.18, a factor of 17.
benchmark: A greenfield kraft lime kiln runs about 300-500 CAD per annual tonne of lime; 887 looks like the Swedish study's full new-kiln-and-fuel-system case rather than a kiln.
recommendation: Read Svensson's investment table back to see what the rotary case includes, and name a host for kiln_lime-rotary in records/fill/host-archetype.csv so the Owttrim and Kuparinen rows can be used. Ask Brad whether the electric-cheaper-than-rotary ordering is one he wants to carry into CIMS.

value-in-db: steam 4.88752 against a total of 4.01588; heat 5.6 against a total of 2.6776
issue: On both archetypes a carrier pooled apart exceeds the all-carrier total, because the carrier is a median of a different set of examples than the total. dryer_steam-heated's steam is a median of 11 examples while the total is UKERC 2013's; dryer_market-pulp's heat is Suhr et al. 2015's single figure, more than twice the IEAGHG total that the archetype's own split uses. The rationale does warn that these rows do not sum, but wide-archetype.csv puts them side by side and a modeller summing carriers will overstate the dryer.
benchmark: A paper dryer section uses about 3.5-4.5 GJ/t and a market-pulp dryer about 2.5-3.5 GJ/t, so the totals are right and the pooled-apart carriers are on a wider scope.
recommendation: Flag pooled-apart carriers in the wide view, or refuse to publish a carrier above the total and set the row aside instead. Also check whether Suhr's 5.6 GJ/t on dryer_market-pulp is the whole drying line rather than the dryer.

issue: The two biomass figures conflict, the guess rationale says so and asks for a re-read, and the electricity row is a 96/4 split invented on top of the conflict. The total is also the highest specific energy consumption in the biofuels family, 15 times the family median, and screen-bounds flags it as above 3 GJ in per GJ out. DEA 2026's cellulosic row (dea_2026_003:fermenter_cellulosic-ethanol@106-cellulosic-ethanol) is the only source for the total and Humbird et al. 2011 for the smaller biomass figure.
benchmark: Cellulosic ethanol uses about 2.2-2.8 GJ of biomass per GJ of ethanol when the lignin burnt for steam and power is counted, and about 1.9-2.1 GJ when only the fermentable feed is. The two sources are on those two scopes and should not be pooled as one total.
recommendation: Re-read the DEA row to settle whether its biomass includes the lignin fuel, keep the two scopes as separate parameters or examples, and withdraw the invented electricity split until the base is settled.

issue: The ccs-host-plus-addon-energy rule writes a carrier row for every carrier in the capture-node pool, so four chemicals capture variants each carry blast-furnace gas, coke-oven gas, by-product gas and hydrogen rows at zero. Sixteen of the thirty-two screen-bounds sec-zero flags in this family are these rows.
benchmark: A chemicals plant with capture has no blast-furnace or coke-oven gas demand; the rows should not exist.
recommendation: Suppress add-on carrier rows whose value is zero and whose carrier the host does not list.

issue: Both were flagged by screen-bounds as a heat-pump COP below 1, and both are right for the device. An absorption heat transformer upgrades waste heat without a compressor and has a COP of 0.3-0.5 by construction, which the archetype description states; a single-effect absorption chiller has a COP of about 0.7. The derived SEC [waste-heat] of 2.08333 GJ/GJ follows correctly from COP 0.48.
benchmark: Absorption heat transformer COP 0.33-0.50; single-effect absorption chiller COP 0.65-0.75 (IEA HPT Annex 58, ASHRAE).
recommendation: No change. Add an exception for heat-transformer and absorption-chiller equipment to the cop-low screen so the flag stops recurring.

issue: A construction time of zero fails the physical bound and feeds the levelized identity. The archetype has one example, so there is nothing to median against.
benchmark: Utility PV with storage: 0.5-1.5 years (DEA 2026, NREL ATB).
recommendation: Exclude the zero row and take the construction time from a sibling, or read the DEA sheet again, which may print months.

issue: The species split works: vapour-recompression now sits on its own secondary row (445 %, n=15) and the closed-cycle pool medians at 350 %, which is right. What is left is the high bound, 1090 %, from tp-rtc_2022_001-0004, a printed COP of 10.9 whose own note says it is a calculated matrix rather than a measured machine. On a closed-cycle pool that stretches the band to COP 10.9.
benchmark: Closed-cycle industrial heat pumps: COP 2.5-4.5 at a 40-80 K lift, up to about 6 at small lifts (IEA HPT Annex 58, DEA 2026).
recommendation: Exclude the RTC calculated-matrix COP rows from the band, or cap the closed-cycle high at about 600 %. The pooling problem itself is closed (S84, S09, R021, R069).

recommendation: As R242: check the Pardo basis and prefer the Daniels carrier split.

issue: Noting against the open item in the brief: moya_2013_001 and pardo_2013_001 touch no cement archetype in this build. Every row from both sources maps to iron and steel (coke oven, sinter, blast furnace, BOF, EAF, rolling and coating), with all 70 Moya rows excluded and the Pardo rows live. issue: Fixed opex is 0.5 % of capex for the gas calciner and 0.2 % for the electric one, and fill-backtest flags all four rows outside the estimate band by 7x to 29x. Both come from mpp_2023_001, where the cost lines may be per t aluminium rather than per t alumina, which would also explain the capex of 110 CAD/t-per-yr.
benchmark: Fixed opex 2.5-10 % of capex per year (the DB's own median ratio is 4.2 %)
recommendation: Check the MPP basis for the calciner cost lines against the 1.93 t alumina per t aluminium factor, and re-extract if they are per t aluminium. Prior finding R370 recorded the electric calciner.

issue: The sourced co2e row sits 0.4% BELOW the identity co2 row (0.381265 t/m3) for the same archetype, which cannot be right for a CO2-equivalent total. The ceri_2017_002 note explains it: the 60.4 kg/bbl is direct natural-gas CO2 only, with flaring, fugitive, and electricity-generation emissions excluded. So the two rows describe the same flow under two target labels and anything that sums them double counts.
benchmark: A SAGD co2e total should exceed its combustion CO2; CERI's own whole-process figure is the emissions-total co2e row of 0.538849 t/m3.
recommendation: Retag the 60.4 kg/bbl row as emissions-combustion co2, or drop it in favour of the identity, and keep the whole-process figure in emissions-total.

issue: Every value on this archetype comes from potash crystallization (gielen_1997_001 per t K2O and nccp_1999_003), so the 7 GJ/t of heat is a thermal potash duty per tonne of K2O. The archetype's own description says "mechanical vapour recompression evaporators", which would be 0.1-0.3 GJ/t of electricity, and the produced-water sibling split off on 2026-10-09 sits at 0.2 GJ/m3, 38x lower for essentially the same quantity of water.
benchmark: MVR brine concentration is 0.1-0.2 GJ/t of water; multi-effect thermal evaporation is 0.3-0.8 GJ/t; 7 GJ/t only makes sense per t of K2O product.
recommendation: Either change the description to match the thermal potash data or move the archetype's lead family to mining, since the oil-and-gas use is now carried by evaporator_crystallizer-produced-water.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The 2026-10-05 fix that sends hours-based lifetimes to a stack or component species works where the source gives hours: haul-truck_hydrogen-fuel-cell has both a component life (2.85 years) and a stack life (4.57 years), and fuel-cell_chp has a stack life of 4.57. This archetype has neither, so its 10-year guess carries the whole machine and the stack together and the model cannot see the stack replacement the rationale mentions.
benchmark: Fuel-cell stack 20,000-30,000 operating hours (about 4-6 years at 5,000 h/yr); chassis 10-15 years
recommendation: Copy the stack species from haul-truck_hydrogen-fuel-cell (or extract the stack hours from the DEA 2026 agricultural-machinery sheets) so the fuel-cell machines carry both lives.

issue: Vakkilainen 2006's main steam pressures all drop out with 'no conversion from bar(g) to bar' and 'no conversion from MPa to bar' (tp-vakkilainen_2006_001-0003, -0007, -0011, -0015, -0019, -0023, -0026, -0028, -0031, -0033, -0036), so the pooled 91 bar rests on Lipiainen, IEAGHG and Sharp alone and the high-solids variant keeps only Suhr's 110 bar.
